definition_zh: 谈话；交谈；会话
definition_en: an informal talk in which people exchange news and feelings
core_image: 两个人面对面，你一句我一句像打乒乓球
scene: 午休时，我和同桌聊起周末的机器人展览。 Our conversation about robots lasted the whole lunch break.
sceneCN: 这里 conversation 是「交谈」（第 1 个义项：两人轮流说话交流）；句意是我们关于机器人的谈话聊了整个午休。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根构成，义为「交谈」
由 conversation 加 -al 构成，义为「口语的；健谈的」
义为「用谈话方式」

senses.title: An informal talk between people
senses.definition: a talk in which people share news, ideas or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 人们交流消息、想法或感受的谈话
senses.example: I had a long conversation with my grandma on the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 我和奶奶在电话里聊了很久。
senses.why: Latin versare means to turn, and a conversation turns from speaker to speaker like a wheel.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 versare 意为转动，交谈像轮子一样在说话人之间轮转。

senses.title: The skill or style of talking
senses.definition: the way someone talks with others
senses.definitionCN: 一个人与人交谈的方式
senses.example: Good conversation makes parties more fun.
senses.exampleCN: 好的谈吐让聚会更有趣。
senses.why: Because talks rotate smoothly, the word also names the manner of the exchange itself.
senses.whyCN: 由于谈话轮转顺畅，这个词也指交流本身的方式。

senses.title: A formal exchange in computing
senses.definition: an exchange between a user and a program or system
senses.definitionCN: 用户与程序系统之间的交互
senses.example: The app keeps a conversation history of your questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用保存你的问答记录。
senses.why: Machine dialogue imitates human turn-taking, so engineers borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 机器对话模仿人类轮流说话，工程师便借用了这个词。

intro.en: Conversation originally meant the act of turning about or living among people.
intro.cn: conversation 最初意为「转身往复；与人共处」。

items.en: The Latin verb conversari meant to live with or keep company, from com- (with) + versare (to turn often).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 conversari 意为与人共处，由 com-（与）+ versare（反复转动）构成。

items.en: conversatio described one's manner of life and behaviour.
items.cn: conversatio 描述一个人的生活方式与举止。

items.en: French carried conversacion with meanings of conduct and company.
items.cn: 法语 conversacion 兼有行为与交往之义。

items.en: English first used conversation for conduct and later for living together.
items.cn: 英语最初用 conversation 表示行为，后指与人交往。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it meant the familiar exchange of words we know today.
items.cn: 到十七世纪它才表示今天熟悉的言谈交流。

note.en: These words share the vers root of turning, or name kinds of talk.
note.cn: 这些词共享 vers（转）词根，或表示各种言谈。

abstract.en: Picture two friends on a bench, laughing in turn.

examples.en: She started a conversation with the new student.

examples.en: Practise conversations with your partner to improve spoken English.

sensesIntro.en: From living together to talking and turn-taking.

branches.en: Good talk is smooth turning.
branches.cn: 好的谈话是顺畅的轮转。

definition_zh: 房间；室；空间；余地
definition_en: a part of a building with walls, or the space needed for something
core_image: 一间空荡的房间
scene: 屋里已经放不下一张更大的桌子了。 There is no room for a larger table in here.

derivatives.zh: 宽敞的
室友
一屋子的人或物

senses.title: Walled space
senses.definition: a part of a building with walls, a floor, and a ceiling
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物中用墙、地板和天花板隔出的一部分
senses.example: The dining room faces the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 餐厅朝向花园。
senses.why: Walls make a separate space inside a house.
senses.whyCN: 墙壁在房子里隔出一块独立空间。

senses.title: Space
senses.definition: the empty space that is available for people or things
senses.definitionCN: 可供人或物使用的空余空间
senses.example: There is little room left in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 车里剩下的空间不多了。
senses.why: The empty area is the same idea without walls.
senses.whyCN: 空出来的区域就是没有墙的空间概念。

senses.title: Scope
senses.definition: the chance or scope for something to happen or improve
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生或改进的机会与余地
senses.example: The plan leaves room for change.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划留有改动的余地。
senses.why: Free space becomes free possibility.
senses.whyCN: 空余空间转成空余可能性。

intro.en: Room comes from Old English rum, meaning spacious.
intro.cn: room 源自古代英语 rum，意为宽敞的。

items.en: Rum means space or a spacious place.
items.cn: rum 意为空间或宽敞之处。

items.en: Rum also describes something wide and open.
items.cn: rum 也形容宽大开阔之物。

items.en: Roum narrows to a part of a house.
items.cn: roum 收窄为房屋中的一个部分。

items.en: Room keeps both the walled and open senses.
items.cn: room 同时保留有墙房间与开放空间两义。

items.en: Room for improvement becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: room for improvement 成为常用短语。

note.en: A room has walls; space is open area.
note.cn: room 通常指有墙的房间，space 则是开放的空间。

normalIntro.en: A room is space you can walk into or use.
normalIntro.cn: room 是你可以走进去或使用的空间。

normal.en: The living room opens onto a small balcony.
normal.cn: 客厅通向一个小阳台。

normal.en: Please make room for the new books.
normal.cn: 请为新书腾出空间。

normal.en: Room service brought breakfast at seven.
normal.cn: 客房服务七点送来了早餐。

normal.en: There is room for improvement in the essay.

abstract.en: Think of an open door leading to a wider place.

examples.en: The room was quiet and full of light.
examples.cn: 房间安静而明亮。

examples.en: We need more room for the guests.
examples.cn: 我们需要更多空间招待客人。

examples.en: There is still room to improve the design.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「room」读音像「如木」——木头隔出的空处就是房间；空着的部分就是空间与余地。

root: 古代英语 rum（宽敞、空间）→ room，核心义「空出来的地方」。

sensesIntro.en: Room means a walled part of a building, available space, or scope for something.
sensesIntro.cn: room 意为有墙的房间、可用空间，或做某事的余地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty room with light on the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光落在地板上的空房间。

branches.en: The walled area is the first sense.
branches.cn: 有墙的空间是第一个义项。

branches.en: Open space needs no walls.
branches.cn: 开放空间并不需要墙。

branches.en: Free space becomes free possibility.

branches.en: Spare room allows things to change.

latinIntro.en: Room has no Latin root; its family is English and Germanic.

definition_zh: 是；存在；成为；处于；发生（用于构成时态与被动）
definition_en: to exist, to have a quality, or to be in a state or place
core_image: 一面镜子里映出的就是眼前这个东西本身
scene: 毕业册上，男孩写下将来的愿望，说想当一名医生。 He wants to be a doctor when he grows up.
sceneCN: 这里 be 是「成为」（第 4 个义项：将来取得某种身份）；句意为他长大后想当一名医生。

pos.zh: 助动词：构成进行时与被动语态

forms.label: 第一与第三人称单数过去式

derivatives.zh: 由 be 加 -ing 构成，义为「存在；生物」
由 may 与 be 组合而成，义为「也许」
由 well 与 being 组合而成，义为「幸福安康」

senses.title: To have a quality or identity
senses.definition: used to link a subject with a noun or adjective that describes it
senses.definitionCN: 用来把主语与描述它的名词或形容词连起来
senses.example: She is a student and her brother is a teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她是学生，她哥哥是老师。
senses.why: The oldest use simply puts two things side by side as the same, so linking subject and description is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法只是把两样东西并排视为同一，所以把主语与描述连起来就是第一义。

senses.title: To exist
senses.definition: to exist or to be present in a place
senses.definitionCN: 存在，或位于某个地方
senses.example: There are three chairs in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里有三把椅子。
senses.why: Before anything can be described, it must simply be there, so existence is the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 任何东西在被描述之前，必须先「在那里」，所以「存在」是第二义。

senses.title: To be in a state
senses.definition: used with an adjective or phrase to describe a temporary state or condition
senses.definitionCN: 与形容词或短语连用，描述暂时的状态或情况
senses.example: He is tired after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 走了很久之后他很累。
senses.why: Identity and existence combine into a state: the thing is here, and here is how it is.
senses.whyCN: 「是什么」与「在那里」合成状态：东西在这里，而且它是这个样子。

senses.title: To become
senses.definition: used in phrases such as be a doctor to mean to become one
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be a doctor 这类说法，表示成为某种身份
senses.example: She wants to be a doctor when she grows up.
senses.exampleCN: 她长大后想当医生。
senses.why: A future identity is spoken of as if it already holds, so being something can also mean becoming it.
senses.whyCN: 未来的身份被说得好像已经成立，所以「是某种人」也能表示「成为某种人」。

senses.title: Auxiliary for tenses and passive
senses.titleCN: 助动词：构成时态与被动
senses.definition: used with a participle to form the continuous tenses or the passive voice
senses.definitionCN: 与分词连用，构成进行时或被动语态
senses.example: The bridge was built last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是去年建成的。
senses.why: Once be can state a condition, it can also hold another verb's action in that condition, which gives the auxiliary use.
senses.whyCN: 既然 be 能陈述状态，它也能把另一个动词的动作放进这个状态里，于是有了助动词用法。

intro.en: Be is the most irregular verb in English because it merged forms from three different old roots.
intro.cn: be 是英语中最不规则的动词，因为它把三个不同古老词根的形式合并在一起。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to grow or to become lies behind the am, is, are forms.
items.cn: 一个可重构、意为「生长、成为」的词根，是 am、is、are 这些形式的远源。

items.en: Old English had beon, to be or to become, and also wesan, to remain or exist.
items.cn: 古英语既有 beon「是、成为」，也有 wesan「存在、停留」。

items.en: The forms am and is come from a different root that meant to exist.
items.cn: am 与 is 来自另一个表示「存在」的词根。

items.en: Middle English joined these sets into one verb, which is why its forms look so unlike each other.
items.cn: 中古英语把这些形式合并成一个动词，所以它的各形式看起来彼此很不相同。

items.en: The auxiliary uses for continuous and passive sentences became standard in later English.
items.cn: 构成进行时与被动句的助动词用法，在后来的英语中成为标准。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the forms of the same verb; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs that express existence or a state.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个动词的各种形式；近义组收表示存在或状态的其他动词。

entries.definition: The third person singular present form of be.
entries.definitionCN: be 的第三人称单数现在时形式。

entries.definition: The present plural form of be, also used with you.
entries.definitionCN: be 的现在时复数形式，也用于第二人称。

entries.definition: The past form of be for I, he, she and it.
entries.definitionCN: be 用于第一、第三人称单数的过去式。

entries.definition: The past participle of be, used after have.
entries.definitionCN: be 的过去分词，用在 have 之后。

entries.definition: To be real or present; a more formal verb for the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「存在」，是第二个义项的正式说法。

entries.definition: To begin to be something; it makes the fourth sense explicit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「成为」，把第四个义项说明得更清楚。

entries.definition: To continue to be in a state; it stresses staying rather than starting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「仍然是」，强调持续而非开始。

entries.definition: To appear to be something, without saying that it truly is.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「似乎」，表示看起来是，而不断言确实是。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real history of the merged forms and the everyday phrases built with be.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这些形式合并的真实历史，以及由 be 构成的日常搭配。

normal.en: Am, is and are come from one old root, while was and were come from another, which is why the verb looks irregular.
normal.cn: am、is、are 来自一个古老词根，was、were 来自另一个，所以这个动词看起来不规则。

normal.en: Been is the past participle, so it appears after have: I have been there.
normal.cn: been 是过去分词，所以出现在 have 之后：I have been there。

normal.en: Being is both the present participle and a noun meaning a living creature.
normal.cn: being 既是现在分词，也是名词，指活着的生物。

normal.en: Be careful and be sure use be plus an adjective to describe a state.
normal.cn: be careful 与 be sure 用 be 加形容词来描述状态。

normal.en: Be from asks about origin, while be at asks about place.
normal.cn: be from 问来源，be at 问地点。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror: it adds nothing to what stands before it, it only says that the thing is.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子：它不给眼前的东西增添什么，只是确认那东西「在」。

abstract.en: The same small word holds identity, place, state, and time, because all four answer the question of what is.
abstract.cn: 同一个小词装着身份、位置、状态与时间，因为四者都在回答「什么在」。

abstract.en: English kept the most-used verb the most irregular, because everyone says it too often to change it.
abstract.cn: 英语把最常用的动词保留得最不规则，因为人人说得太多，反而改不动它。

examples.en: She is a student and her brother is a teacher.
examples.cn: 她是学生，她哥哥是老师。

examples.en: There are three chairs in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里有三把椅子。

examples.en: The bridge was built last year.
examples.cn: 这座桥是去年建成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必」——必定在那里，才谈得上是什么：是、存在

root: be 由三个古老词源合并而成：beon「是、成为」、wesan「存在、停留」，以及给出 am、is 的另一个「存在」词根；可上溯到原始印欧语重构形式。中古英语把这些形式并成一个动词，因此变位极不规则。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of be all answer what is: what something is, that it exists, how it is, what it will become, and what is done to it.
sensesIntro.cn: be 的五个义项都在回答「什么在」：某物是什么、它存在、它处于什么状态、它将变成什么，以及它被做了什么。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror shows the object in front of it exactly as it is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面镜子把眼前的东西原样映出来。

branches.en: THE IDENTITY: the verb links a subject with what it is.
branches.cn: 身份线：这个动词把主语与它是什么连起来。

branches.en: THE EXISTENCE: before description, the thing must simply be there.
branches.cn: 存在线：在被描述之前，东西必须先在那里。

branches.en: THE STATE: identity plus place gives a temporary condition.
branches.cn: 状态线：身份加位置合成暂时的状况。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: a future identity is spoken of as already true.
branches.cn: 变化线：未来的身份被说成已经成立。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR: the same verb carries other actions through time and into the passive.
branches.cn: 语法线：同一个动词把别的动作带过时间，并带进被动语态。

intro.en: Be is a root verb rather than a derived word; its family comes from merged forms and compounds like maybe.
intro.cn: be 是根动词而非派生词，它的词族来自合并的各种形式以及 maybe 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The English verb is Germanic; Latin had its own verb esse, which is not a cognate of be, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个英语动词属日耳曼语；拉丁语另有动词 esse「是」，并非 be 的同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.meaning: to be, exist, or have a quality

items.meaning: used for I, he, she, it in the past

definition_zh: 膝；膝盖；膝部；裤子的膝部
definition_en: the joint between the thigh and the lower leg, the front part of that joint, or the part of a garment covering it
core_image: 一条腿在弯折处凸起的硬骨，屈伸之间承担全身重量
scene: 球场上有人被铲倒，抱着腿蜷在草皮上。 He fell on his knee and stayed down for a moment before standing up again.
sceneCN: 这里 knee 是「膝盖、膝关节」（第 1 个义项：大腿与小腿之间的关节），句意是他跪倒在地，停了一会儿才重新站起来。画面里有球场草皮与受伤的球员。

pos.zh: 名词：膝；膝关节；膝部；裤膝

derivatives.zh: 与 knee 同源的动词，义为「跪下」
knee 与 deep 合成，义为「深及膝盖的」
knee 与 cap 合成，义为「膝盖骨」
合成词，义为「条件反射式的、不经思考的」

senses.title: The joint of the leg
senses.definition: the joint where the thigh and the lower leg meet, which allows the leg to bend
senses.definitionCN: 大腿与小腿相接、能让腿弯曲的关节
senses.example: The old injury still makes his knee ache in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 旧伤让他的膝盖一到冷天就疼。
senses.why: The joint is the body part the word first named, and all other senses grow from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早命名的就是这处关节，其他义项都由它生长出来。

senses.title: The front of the knee
senses.definition: the front area of the leg around that joint, where a person kneels
senses.definitionCN: 关节周围的腿部前侧，人下跪时着地的部位
senses.example: She rested the baby on her knee.
senses.exampleCN: 她把婴儿放在膝上。
senses.why: Because the front of the joint is what people rest things on, the same word names the lap-like surface.
senses.whyCN: 由于关节前侧是人放东西的地方，同一个词也用来指这块近似膝盖上的台面。

senses.title: The part of a garment over the knee
senses.definition: the part of a trouser leg that covers the knee
senses.definitionCN: 裤腿上覆盖膝盖的那一段
senses.example: The boy always wore out the knees of his trousers.
senses.exampleCN: 那男孩总把裤子的膝部磨破。
senses.why: Clothing takes the names of the body parts it covers, so trousers have knees as people do.
senses.whyCN: 衣物会借用它所覆盖的身体部位之名，所以裤子也有膝盖。

intro.en: Knee is an old Germanic body word whose k has been silent for centuries; related words survive in German and Dutch.
intro.cn: knee 是古老的日耳曼语身体词，词首的 k 已沉默数百年；相关词在德语与荷兰语中留存。

items.en: The noun was cneo, and the related verb cneowian meant to kneel.
items.cn: 名词写作 cneo，相关的动词 cneowian 意为「跪下」。

items.en: German Knie and Dutch knie show the same word in the other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 德语 Knie 与荷兰语 knie 显示同一词在日耳曼语其他分支中的样貌。

items.en: The spelling became kne and knes, and the k stopped being pronounced before the vowel.
items.cn: 拼法变为 kne 与 knes，词首的 k 在元音前已不再发音。

items.en: The silent k and the long vowel make knee look unlike the way it sounds.
items.cn: 不发音的 k 与长元音让 knee 的写法与读音显得很不一样。

items.en: English builds compounds from it, among them kneecap and knee-deep.
items.cn: 英语用它构成合成词，如 kneecap 与 knee-deep。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same silent k or a similar ending; the near-meaning group gathers other joints and related body words.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带不发音 k 或结尾相近的词；近义组收其他关节与相关身体词。

entries.definition: The verb from the same Old English root, meaning to go down on the knees.
entries.definitionCN: 与 knee 同出古英语词根的动词，义为「跪」。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k, but means to work dough with the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，意为用手揉面团。

entries.definition: Another silent-k word, naming a cutting tool.
entries.definitionCN: 又一个 k 不发音的词，指刀具。

entries.definition: The part of the leg above the knee.
entries.definitionCN: 膝以上的那段腿，即大腿。

entries.definition: The front of the lower leg below the knee.
entries.definitionCN: 膝以下小腿的前面。

entries.definition: The joint of the arm, the knee of the upper limb.
entries.definitionCN: 手臂的关节，上肢的「膝」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English form, the silent k, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的古英语词形、不发音的 k，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: Old English cneo already had the k, which later went silent.
normal.cn: 古英语 cneo 本就带 k，后来这个音沉默了。

normal.en: German Knie keeps the k spoken, while English dropped the sound.
normal.cn: 德语 Knie 仍把 k 读出来，英语则把它丢掉。

normal.en: On one knee is the pose of a proposal or of rest.
normal.cn: on one knee 是求婚或歇息时的姿势。

normal.en: Kneecap and knee-deep are built straight from the body part.
normal.cn: kneecap 与 knee-deep 直接由这个身体部位构成。

normal.en: Trousers wear out at the knees, exactly where the body bends.
normal.cn: 裤子总在膝部磨破，那里正是身体弯折之处。

abstract.en: A knee is a hinge: the whole body weight travels through a joint the size of a fist.
abstract.cn: 膝盖是一处铰链：全身重量都经过这样一个拳头大小的关节。

abstract.en: The word is the same for the joint, the lap and the cloth over it, because clothing follows the body.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指关节、膝上，也指膝上的布，因为衣物是跟着身体走的。

abstract.en: Bending the knee is the oldest gesture of respect, which is why the verb kneel carries such weight.
abstract.cn: 屈膝是最古老的敬意姿态，所以动词 kneel 才有那样的分量。

examples.en: He hurt his knee during the match.
examples.cn: 他在比赛中伤到了膝盖。

examples.en: The child sat on her father knee and listened.
examples.cn: 孩子坐在父亲膝上听着。

examples.en: These trousers have reinforced knees.
examples.cn: 这条裤子的膝部做了加固。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泥」——跪在泥里，最先沾泥的就是膝盖

root: 古英语 cneo（膝），源自共同日耳曼语，同源于德语 Knie、荷兰语 knie；中古英语作 kne，词首 k 在元音前逐渐不发音，现代英语扩展出 kneecap、knee-deep 等合成词。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the joint itself, the lap-like front of it, and the part of a garment that covers it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：关节本身，关节前侧那块像膝上的台面，以及覆盖它的那段衣料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard knob at the bend of the leg, carrying the body as it folds.
core.cn: 核心意象：腿弯处一块坚硬的凸起，在身体折叠时承担重量。

branches.en: THE JOINT: the hinge where thigh and shin meet.
branches.cn: 关节线：大腿与小腿相接的铰链。

branches.en: THE LAP: the front of the joint is where children and books rest.
branches.cn: 膝上线：关节前侧是放孩子、放书的地方。

branches.en: THE CLOTH: garments take the name of the body part they cover.
branches.cn: 布料线：衣物借用它所覆盖的身体部位之名。

branches.en: THE SOUND LINE: the silent k marks the Germanic history of the word.
branches.cn: 读音线：不发音的 k 标出了这个词的日耳曼来历。

branches.en: THE POSTURE LINE: kneeling and sitting on the knee both begin at this joint.
branches.cn: 姿态线：下跪与坐在膝上，都从这处关节开始。

intro.en: Knee is an inherited Germanic noun; its family is built by inflection and by compounds such as kneecap.
intro.cn: knee 是继承而来的日耳曼名词，其词族靠词形变化以及 kneecap 一类合成构成。

latinIntro.cn: knee 没有拉丁语来源，下面这些拉丁语关节词仅作对照。

definition_zh: 除…之外；除了；要不是；只是
definition_en: not including; used before a statement that forms an exception to what has just been said
core_image: 从一把抓起的东西里松开一只手：大家都在里面，只有它被放出去
scene: 全家出游的合影人人都在笑，只有被留下看家的狗趴在门口，主人叹了口气说： Everyone went to the park except the dog.
sceneCN: 这里 except 指「把某物排除在外」（第 1 个义项：不包含在所谈范围之内）；句意为大家都去了公园，只有狗没去。

derivatives.zh: 例外（except 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「被拿出去的那一件」）
例外的；杰出的（exception 加形容词后缀，义为「作为例外的，进而指超出常格的」）
接受；收下（拼写相近的近亲词，义为「收进来」）

senses.title: Not included in a statement
senses.titleCN: 不包含在所谈范围之内
senses.definition: used before naming the one person or thing that is left out of a general statement
senses.definitionCN: 用在一般性说法之前，点出被排除在外的那个人或物
senses.example: Everyone went to the park except the dog.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都去了公园，只有狗没去。
senses.why: The root image is grabbing with the hand: from everything taken in, one item is caught and lifted out.
senses.whyCN: 词根画面是用手抓取：在全部纳入的东西里，有一件被单独拎了出来。

senses.title: Apart from the mentioned fact
senses.definition: used to add the one fact that is different from what has been said
senses.definitionCN: 补充与前面说法不同的一点
senses.example: I would join you except that I have homework.
senses.exampleCN: 我本想跟你去，只是我有作业。
senses.why: When the excluded item is a whole clause, the hand keeps holding everything but this one part of reality.
senses.whyCN: 当被排除的对象是一整句话时，那只手仍然抓着一切，只是松开现实中这一块。

senses.title: Only; nothing but
senses.definition: used after nothing, all, or only to say what remains
senses.definitionCN: 用在 nothing、all、only 之后，表示仅剩的内容
senses.example: There was nothing in the box except old letters.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子里除了几封旧信什么都没有。
senses.why: Reversing the view: instead of naming what leaves, the sentence names the single thing that stays inside the hand.
senses.whyCN: 换个视角：不说谁出去了，而说手里留下的仅有那一件事物。

senses.title: To leave out deliberately (formal verb)
senses.definition: to leave out or exclude from a general statement or rule
senses.definitionCN: 把某人某物从一般陈述或规则中排除
senses.example: The rule excepts members of the royal family.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款把王室成员排除在外。
senses.why: The verb keeps the literal hand-action: the rule itself reaches out and sets the item aside.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了字面上的手部动作：规则本身伸手把这一项挪开。

intro.en: Except grows from a Latin verb about seizing and taking out, through French, into a word about exclusion.
intro.cn: except 由拉丁语「抓住、取出」义的动词经法语演变而来，最终成为表示排除的词。

items.en: Latin excipere meant "to take out, to except", from ex- (out) + capere (to take, to seize).
items.cn: 拉丁语 excipere 意为「取出、排除」，由 ex-（向外）+ capere（拿、抓住）构成。

items.en: In legal Latin, excipere meant to single out a case so it fell outside a rule; this legal flavour stayed with the word.
items.cn: 在法律拉丁语里，excipere 指把一个情形单独拎出、使之不落入规则，法律色彩随之保留下来。

items.en: Old French took it as excepter, keeping the senses of removing and objecting.
items.cn: 古法语作 excepter，保留「移除」「提出异议」两义。

items.en: Middle English borrowed excepter in the fourteenth century as a verb and preposition together.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语借入 excepter，动词与介词用法同时进入。

items.en: Modern English kept the preposition except and the conjunction except that, while the verb except survived mostly in legal prose.
items.cn: 现代英语保留介词 except 与连词 except that，动词 except 主要存于法律文体。

note.en: Except is easy to confuse with its sibling accept, and sits near other excluding words.
note.cn: except 极易与同源的 accept 混淆，也与另几个排除类词相邻。

entries.definition: to take what is offered willingly
entries.definitionCN: 接受（前缀不同：ac- 向内收，except 是向外拿）

entries.definition: to think something will happen
entries.definitionCN: 预料；期待（拼写相近，词根为 spectare「看」）

entries.definition: a case that does not follow the rule
entries.definitionCN: 例外（同根名词）

entries.definition: a passage taken out of a text
entries.definitionCN: 摘录；节选（同根，取「抽出」义）

entries.definition: in addition to; apart from
entries.definitionCN: 除…之外（还有）；加上的口吻与 except 相反

entries.definition: not counting
entries.definitionCN: 不包括（正式书面）

entries.definition: except for; in addition to
entries.definitionCN: 除…之外（口语常用，方向视语境而定）

normalIntro.en: Five associations from the real root family and usage patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 五条来自真实词根词族与用法的联想。

normal.en: ex- (out) + cept (take): one thing is taken out of the group.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向外）+ 词根 cept（拿）：有一件东西从整体里被拿出去。

normal.en: Exception is the noun: being late is the exception, not the rule.
normal.cn: exception 是名词：迟到是例外，不是常规。

normal.en: Accept points inward (receive), except points outward (exclude) — ac- versus ex-.
normal.cn: accept 向内（收下），except 向外（排除）——区别就在 ac- 与 ex-。

normal.en: Except for is the handy preposition: the essay is good except for one spelling.
normal.cn: except for 是顺手的介词：这篇作文很好，只是有一个拼写错误。

normal.en: Except that opens a whole clause: fine, except that it rains tomorrow.
normal.cn: except that 引导整句：都挺好，只是明天下雨。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of marbles: the fingers open and one marble drops out.
abstract.cn: 想象一把抓着弹珠的手：手指松开，一颗弹珠掉了出去。

abstract.en: The general statement is the closed hand; except is the moment of release.
abstract.cn: 一般性陈述是合拢的手，except 就是松手的那一下。

abstract.en: Exceptions draw boundaries: a rule only shows its edge where except cuts it.
abstract.cn: 例外画出边界：规则正是在 except 切开的地方露出边缘。

examples.cn: 大家都去了公园，只有狗没去。

examples.en: I would join you except that I have homework.
examples.cn: 我本想跟你去，只是我有作业。

examples.en: There was nothing in the box except old letters.
examples.cn: 盒子里除了几封旧信什么都没有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗塞普特」——一颗珠子被塞出来另放一边，剩下的都是「除…之外」。

root: 源自拉丁语 excipere「取出、排除」，由 ex-（向外）+ capere（拿、抓住）构成；法律拉丁语中指把情形单独拎出规则之外。经古法语 excepter 进入中古英语。

sensesIntro.en: From the hand that grabs everything, one item is released: exclusion first, then the leftover that remains.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「抓住一切」的手出发，松开一件即排除，反向看则只剩留下的那一项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one item released from a closed hand
core.cn: 核心意象：合拢的手里松开一件东西

branches.en: the item is formally left out
branches.cn: 该项被正式排除在外

branches.en: a whole clause is the released piece
branches.cn: 被松开的是一整句话

branches.en: what stays inside the hand is named
branches.cn: 点出手上仅剩的那一项

branches.en: exclusion and residue are two views of one cut
branches.cn: 排除与剩余是同一切口的两面

branches.en: the cut can limit or carve out a rule
branches.cn: 这个切口可以限定或豁免规则

intro.en: The family gathers around the Latin root cap- (take, seize) with direction prefixes.
intro.cn: 词族围绕拉丁词根 cap-（拿、抓住）加上方向前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins that keep the cap- root.
latinIntro.cn: 保留 cap- 词根的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 分钟；片刻；会议记录；极小的；细微的
definition_en: a unit of time equal to sixty seconds; a short moment; the written record of a meeting; and, with a different pronunciation, extremely small or very detailed
core_image: 桌上小钟的秒针走完一圈，一小时被切成六十个小格
scene: 会议室门口，秘书把一叠记录纸递过来说人已到齐，主席却还在楼梯上。 The chair opened the meeting a minute late.
sceneCN: 这里是「分钟」（第 1 个义项：时间单位）；句意为主席晚了很短的时间才宣布开会。图中可辨识物件：记录纸、会议室门牌、秒针。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 minute 加 -ly 构成，义为「细微地；精确地」，读作长音
由形容词 minute 加 -ness 构成，义为「微小；精细」
拉丁语 minutia 的复数，与 minute 同出 minutus（变小），义为「细枝末节」

senses.title: A unit of sixty seconds
senses.definition: a period of time equal to sixty seconds, one sixtieth of an hour
senses.definitionCN: 等于六十秒的一段时间，即一小时的六十分之一
senses.example: The film runs ninety minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片放映九十分钟。
senses.why: Latin named this unit pars minuta prima, the first small part of an hour, and the adjective minutus, made small, is the part English kept as the name of the unit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语把这个单位叫作 pars minuta prima，即「一小时的第一小部分」，其中表示「变小」的形容词 minutus 被英语保留下来，成了这个时间单位的名字。

senses.title: A short, indefinite stretch of time
senses.definition: a very short period of time, often used loosely rather than as exactly sixty seconds
senses.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间，常是模糊的说法，而不是精确的六十秒
senses.example: Wait a minute, I left the keys inside.
senses.exampleCN: 等一下，我把钥匙落在里面了。
senses.why: Once a minute names a small division of the hour, it can stand for any brief interval, because the word has already been marked as small.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 minute 指小时里的一小格，它就能代表任何短暂的间隔，因为这个词本身已经被标记成「小」。

senses.title: Extremely small in size
senses.definition: extremely small, so small that it is easy to overlook
senses.definitionCN: 极其小，小到容易被忽略
senses.example: The cracks in the glass were minute and hard to see.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃上的裂纹极小，很难看清。
senses.why: The adjective came straight from Latin minutus, made small, and it kept the literal sense of size while the noun moved off to the clock; English also gives it a long vowel, which is why the two senses sound different.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接来自拉丁语 minutus（变小），保留了字面上的尺寸义，而名词则走去指钟表上的单位；英语还让形容词读长音，所以两种义项听起来不同。

senses.title: Very detailed and precise
senses.definition: done with close attention to small details, as in a minute account or a minute examination
senses.definitionCN: 对细小之处极为留意的，如细致的叙述或细致的检查
senses.example: The report gives a minute account of the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对实验作了极为细致的记述。
senses.why: If something is so small that it needs a close look, then a close look is what the adjective also describes, so from tiny size the word slides to care about tiny detail.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物小到必须凑近才看得清，那么这种凑近的查看本身也能被同一个形容词描述，于是词义从「尺寸极小」滑向「对细处极用心」。

senses.title: The official record of a meeting
senses.definition: the written notes of what was said and decided at a meeting, usually kept in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 会议上发言与决定的书面记录，通常用复数
senses.example: The secretary took the minutes in shorthand.
senses.exampleCN: 秘书用速记做会议记录。
senses.why: Early clerks wrote the record of a meeting in very small script to save paper, and the Latin word for small gave both the script and the record its name, which is why the notes are minutes.
senses.whyCN: 早期文书为了省纸，把会议记录写得很小，拉丁语中表示「小」的词同时给了这种小字和记录本身一个名字，所以记录叫 minutes。

intro.en: Minute carries two histories in one spelling: a Latin adjective meaning made small gave both the clock unit and the adjective, and English separated them by pronunciation.
intro.cn: minute 一个拼写里装着两段历史：拉丁语中表示「变小」的形容词既生出钟表单位，也生出形容词，英语用读音把它们分开了。

items.en: Minutus meant made small, a participle of the verb minuere, to lessen, and it described anything reduced in size.
items.cn: minutus 意为「被弄小的」，是动词 minuere（减少）的分词，用来描述任何被缩小的东西。

items.en: The phrase pars minuta prima, first small part, named one sixtieth of an hour and one sixtieth of a degree, and the small-part word was carried into the unit.
items.cn: 短语 pars minuta prima 意为「第一小部分」，指一小时的六十分之一与一度的六十分之一，这个「小部分」的词后来进入了单位名称。

items.en: Old French used minute for a small written note, especially the clerk's draft of a legal or official record.
items.cn: 古法语用 minute 指小字写的便条，尤指文书对法律或公务记录的草稿。

items.en: Middle English minute named both the sixtieth of an hour and a brief moment, while the adjective small sense entered from written Latin.
items.cn: 中古英语的 minute 既指一小时的六十分之一，也指短暂的片刻；表示「小」的形容词义则从书面拉丁语进入。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun with a short vowel, the adjective with a long vowel, and the plural minutes for the record of a meeting.
items.cn: 现代英语让名词读短音、形容词读长音，并用复数 minutes 指会议记录。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root of smallness through derived adverbs and nouns; the near-meaning group gathers other words for short stretches of time.
note.cn: 形近组顺着表示「小」的拉丁词根，收派生副词与名词；近义组收其他表示短暂时间的词。

entries.definition: In tiny detail; with close attention to small parts.
entries.definitionCN: 以极细的程度；对细部极为留意地。

entries.definition: The quality of being extremely small.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的性质。

entries.definition: Extremely small, or a word form marking smallness.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；指小的词形。

entries.definition: The Latin verb meaning to lessen, listed here for the root only.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语动词「减少」，此处仅列词根。

entries.definition: A very short period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间。

entries.definition: A unit of time equal to one sixtieth of a minute.
entries.definitionCN: 等于一分钟六十分之一的时间单位。

entries.definition: A single point in time, or a very brief moment.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻；极短的瞬间。

entries.definition: A period of time, usually short and vague.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间，通常短暂而模糊。

normalIntro.en: One Latin adjective for small feeds two separate words, so the family splits between clock time, tiny size and the paper record of a meeting.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「小」的拉丁形容词喂出两条不同的词路，词族因此分到钟表时间、极小尺寸与会议纸面记录。

normal.en: The time unit began as pars minuta prima, the first small part of an hour, so minute literally names a small slice of time.
normal.cn: 这个时间单位起初是 pars minuta prima，即「一小时的第一小部分」，所以 minute 字面上就是时间的一小片。

normal.en: The adjective keeps the Latin sense of minutus, made small, and English marks it with a long vowel so the ear can tell it from the clock word.
normal.cn: 形容词保留了拉丁语 minutus（变小）的意思，英语用长音标记它，让耳朵能把它与钟表那个词分开。

normal.en: Minutes of a meeting were first notes written in small script, which is why the official record shares the spelling of the small adjective.
normal.cn: 会议记录最初是用小字写下的笔记，所以正式记录与小这个形容词共用同一个拼写。

normal.en: Minutely and minuteness belong to the small adjective rather than to the time noun, and their vowels show which branch they come from.
normal.cn: minutely 与 minuteness 属于「小」的形容词，而不是时间名词，它们的元音显示了自己来自哪一支。

normal.en: Diminutive comes from the same Latin verb minuere, to lessen, so the whole family keeps returning to shrinking.
normal.cn: diminutive 出自同一个拉丁动词 minuere（减少），整个词族不断回到「缩小」这个动作。

abstract.en: Picture a clock face cut into sixty thin slices, then one slice held up close enough to show its scratches.
abstract.cn: 想象钟面被切成六十片薄片，然后取一片凑近到能看清上面的划痕。

abstract.en: The same word measures the hour and the speck of dust: smallness is the thread joining the clock to the microscope.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量一小时，也量一粒尘：小是把钟表与显微镜串起来的那根线。

abstract.en: A meeting becomes a few written pages, and those pages are named after the smallness of the handwriting that saved paper.
abstract.cn: 一场会议变成几页纸，而这几页纸得名于当初为省纸而写的小字。

examples.en: The train leaves in a minute.
examples.cn: 列车一分钟后开。

examples.en: The letters on the coin were minute and hard to read.
examples.cn: 硬币上的字母极小，很难辨认。

examples.en: She took the minutes at every board meeting.
examples.cn: 每次董事会都由她做记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你特」——迷你的本子很小，翻一页只花一分钟；记住 minute 既指分钟，也指微小的。

root: 拉丁语 minutus（变小，出自 minuere「减少」）；时间义来自 pars minuta prima（一小时的第一小部分），形容词义直接来自 minutus；会议记录义经古法语 minute（小字记录）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small piece of the hour; the senses divide into the clock unit, the vague short moment, the tiny size kept by the adjective, the close detail that size demands, and the small-script record of a meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「小时里的一小片」；义项分到钟表单位、模糊的短暂片刻、形容词保留的极小尺寸、小尺寸所要求的细致，以及用小字写成的会议记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small clock hand sweeping a circle cut into sixty narrow slices.
core.cn: 核心意象：小小的钟表指针扫过被切成六十个窄格的圆盘。

branches.en: a clock face divided into sixty slices
branches.cn: 钟面被分成六十格

branches.en: someone holding a door and saying just a moment
branches.cn: 有人扶住门说再等一下

branches.en: a crack too thin for the eye to catch
branches.cn: 细得眼睛看不见的裂纹

branches.en: a page of notes on the smallest parts of a test
branches.cn: 一页记着实验最细处的笔记

branches.en: a clerk writing the meeting in tiny script
branches.cn: 文书用小字记下会议

intro.en: Latin words for small and to lessen supply the stem, and English suffixes build the adverb, the quality noun and the family word for a small form.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「小」与「减少」的词提供词干，英语后缀则造出副词、性质名词，以及与「指小」相关的词族成员。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: first small part of an hour

definition_zh: 如果；是否；假如；即使（让步）
definition_en: used to introduce a condition, a doubt or an indirect question
core_image: 站在岔路口说：先看另一边会怎样
scene: 妈妈望着窗外的乌云。 If it rains, we will move the picnic indoors.
sceneCN: 这里 if 是「如果」（第 1 个义项：引导条件从句）；句意：如果下雨，我们就把野餐挪到室内。

derivatives.zh: 当且仅当（数学用语）；缩合形式
假设性设想；复合构词

senses.title: Introducing a condition
senses.definition: used to say that one thing depends on another
senses.definitionCN: 表示一事取决于另一事
senses.example: If you finish early, call me.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你提前做完，给我打电话。
senses.why: The word opens a fork in the road: what happens depends on which branch is real.
senses.whyCN: 这个词打开岔路口：结果取决于哪条岔路成真。

senses.title: Introducing an indirect question
senses.definition: used after verbs like ask or wonder, meaning whether
senses.definitionCN: 用于 ask、wonder 等动词后，意为是否
senses.example: She asked if the shop was open.
senses.exampleCN: 她问商店开没开门。
senses.why: The fork becomes a genuine question: either answer may be true.
senses.whyCN: 岔路变成真正的疑问：两种答案都可能为真。

senses.title: Concession: even if
senses.definition: used to say something is true regardless of the condition
senses.definitionCN: 表示无论条件如何某事都成立
senses.example: Even if it costs more, we will buy it.
senses.exampleCN: 即使更贵，我们也会买。
senses.why: Both forks lead to the same place: the result does not change.
senses.whyCN: 两条岔路通向同一处：结果不变。

senses.title: Wish or regret: if only
senses.titleCN: 愿望与遗憾：要是……就好了
senses.definition: used to express a strong wish about an unreal situation
senses.definitionCN: 表达对不真实情境的强烈愿望
senses.example: If only I had studied harder.
senses.exampleCN: 要是当初更用功就好了。
senses.why: The speaker stares at the road not taken and aches for it.
senses.whyCN: 说话者凝望着那条没走的路，为之怅然。

senses.title: Although or as if in comparisons
senses.definition: in as if, describing how something appears or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 在 as if 中描述事物呈现的样子
senses.example: He talked as if he owned the place.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话好像他是这里的主人。
senses.why: One road is imagined as a mirror of the real one.
senses.whyCN: 一条岔路被想象成现实道路的镜像。

intro.en: If comes from Old English gif, of Germanic origin, related to Old High German ibu and Old Norse ef. It may descend from a particle meaning so that or even so, but the deeper root is uncertain.
intro.cn: if 来自古英语 gif，属日耳曼源，与古高地德语 ibu、古诺斯语 ef 相关；或出自意指「以便、即便如此」的小词，更深词根不确定。

items.en: The Germanic family gives Old Norse ef and Old High German ibu alongside Old English gif.
items.cn: 日耳曼语族给出古诺斯语 ef 与古高地德语 ibu，与古英语 gif 并列。

items.en: Old English gif already covered conditions, doubts and concessions in law codes and poetry.
items.cn: 古英语 gif 在法典与诗歌中已涵盖条件、疑问与让步用法。

items.en: Middle English if standardized in spelling and fixed the indirect-question use after ask and know.
items.cn: 中古英语统一拼写 if，固定了 ask、know 后接间接疑问的用法。

items.en: Early modern English added the unreal wish if only and the concessive even if.
items.cn: 近代英语加入虚拟愿望 if only 与让步 even if。

items.en: Modern English built compounds and phrases: what-if, iffy, as if.
items.cn: 现代英语构成复合词与短语：what-if、iffy、as if。

note.en: The look-alike group lists short conditional words. The meaning group compares other ways of opening a condition or doubt.
note.cn: 形近组列出短小的条件词；词义组比较其他引出条件或疑问的方式。

entries.definition: uncertain or doubtful; an adjective built from if.
entries.definitionCN: 不确定的。由 if 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: a preposition. Two letters apart but no relation.
entries.definitionCN: 介词。只差一个字母，毫无关系。

entries.definition: a negative condition word, meaning if not.
entries.definitionCN: 除非。表否定条件。

entries.definition: used for indirect questions and choices; more formal than if.
entries.definitionCN: 是否。间接疑问中比 if 更正式。

entries.definition: introducing a condition, often a restriction.
entries.definitionCN: 以……为条件。常带限制意味。

entries.definition: in inverted conditionals like should you need help.
entries.definitionCN: 在倒装条件句中表假设，如 should you need help。

normalIntro.en: These hooks lean on the fork-in-the-road image, the fixed phrases and the little traps around of and whether.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩依托岔路口意象、固定短语，以及 of 与 whether 的易混陷阱。

normal.en: if is a fork in the road: first picture both branches.
normal.cn: if 是岔路口：先想象两条岔路。

normal.en: if only stares at the road not taken.
normal.cn: if only 凝望着那条没走的路。

normal.en: even if closes the fork: both roads lead to the same result.
normal.cn: even if 关闭岔路：两条路通向同一结果。

normal.en: Do not confuse if and of; only one opens a condition.
normal.cn: 别混淆 if 和 of；只有一个能打开条件。

normal.en: After ask and wonder, if can mean whether.
normal.cn: 在 ask、wonder 后，if 可以表「是否」。

abstract.en: One image: a signpost with two blank arrows.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一块立着两支空白箭头的路牌。

abstract.en: If is the smallest word that builds whole alternate worlds.
abstract.cn: if 是最小的词，却能搭建整个平行世界。

abstract.en: Grammar feels the fork: real conditions use present tense, dreams use were.
abstract.cn: 语法感受岔路：真实条件用现在时，梦想用 were。

examples.en: If you need help, just raise your hand.
examples.cn: 如果需要帮助，举手就好。

examples.en: I wonder if the museum closes on Mondays.
examples.cn: 不知道博物馆周一闭不闭馆。

examples.en: If only the weather had been kinder.
examples.cn: 要是天气再好一点就好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一分」：如果考试多一分，我就能进决赛——一切从「如果」开始。

root: 古英语 gif「如果」，日耳曼语源，与古诺斯语 ef、古高地德语 ibu 同族；更深词根不确定。派生形容词 iffy 及复合词 what-if 为后世发展。

sensesIntro.en: If opens roads: a real condition, an indirect doubt, a concession that closes the fork, a wish for the road not taken, and an imagined mirror of reality.
sensesIntro.cn: if 打开道路：真实条件、间接疑问、关闭岔路的让步、对未走之路的愿望，以及对现实的想象镜像。

core.en: A fork opened in speech: reality may take either branch.
core.cn: 在语言中打开的岔路口：现实可以走任意一条岔路。

branches.en: CONDITION: if you finish early.
branches.cn: 条件：如果你提前完成。

branches.en: DOUBT: asked if the shop was open.
branches.cn: 疑问：问商店是否开门。

branches.en: CONCESSION: even if it costs more.
branches.cn: 让步：即使更贵。

branches.en: WISH: if only I had studied.
branches.cn: 愿望：要是当初学过就好了。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: as if he owned the place.
branches.cn: 仿佛：as if 他是这里的主人。

intro.en: If builds few descendants, but iffy, what-if and the set phrases carry the little word far.
intro.cn: if 的后代不多，但 iffy、what-if 及各种固定短语让这个小词走得很远。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty: if is a Germanic function word with no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空：if 是日耳曼语功能词，与拉丁语无亲缘。

items.example: If the door is locked, knock twice.
If only we had left earlier.
items.exampleCN: 要是我们早点出发就好了。

items.example: She smiled as if nothing happened.
items.exampleCN: 她微笑着，仿佛什么都没发生。

items.example: Even if it rains, we go.

items.exampleCN: 该计划覆盖了各种假设情形。

items.example: The proof holds iff the matrix is square.
items.exampleCN: 仅当矩阵为方阵时证明成立。

items.example: Will you come? If so, reply today.
items.exampleCN: 你会来吗？如果来，今天回复。

definition_zh: 今晚；今夜；今晚的（活动）
definition_en: the night or evening of the present day, or during that night
core_image: 街上灯一盏盏亮起来，剧场门口的灯箱写着今晚的场次
scene: 厨房里碗刚洗完，桌上还留着两杯热茶，窗外的天已经黑透了。 The concert is tonight, so we should leave before seven.
sceneCN: 这里 tonight 指「今晚这一夜」（第 1 个义项：今天晚上的时间）；句意为音乐会就在今晚，我们七点前该出发。画面里有夜色、洗好的碗与等着出门的动作。

derivatives.zh: 同一构词模式的同族词，义为「今天」
同一构词模式的同族词，义为「明天」
构成词后半部分的名词，义为「夜晚」

senses.title: The night of today
senses.definition: the night or evening that follows the present day
senses.definitionCN: 今天之后的那个夜晚或傍晚
senses.example: We are staying in tonight because of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 因为暴风雨，我们今晚待在家里。
senses.why: The word is a preposition fused to night, so it points at the dark part of the current day.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是介词与 night 的融合，指向当天的黑暗时段。

senses.title: During the coming night
senses.definition: as an adverb, during the night that follows today
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时指在今天之后的那一夜里
senses.example: The temperature will fall below zero tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚气温会降到零度以下。
senses.why: As an adverb the word needs no preposition, which is why we say tonight rather than in tonight.
senses.whyCN: 作副词时这个词不带介词，所以只说 tonight 而不说 in tonight。

senses.title: A scheduled event for today
senses.definition: the arrangement, programme, or performance set for the present evening
senses.definitionCN: 安排在今晚的活动、节目或演出
senses.example: Tonight's match has been moved to the smaller ground.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚的比赛已经改到较小的球场。
senses.why: With the possessive the word works as a noun, and that shift lets it label an event rather than a time.
senses.whyCN: 加所有格后它充当名词，这一转变使它能够标示一场活动而非一段时间。

senses.title: The present evening as a unit of plans
senses.definition: the present evening considered as the block of time available for plans
senses.definitionCN: 把今晚看作可用来安排事情的一段时间
senses.example: I have the whole of tonight to finish the chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 我有一整晚的时间读完这一章。
senses.why: Once it names a block of hours, the word can take quantity phrases like the whole of.
senses.whyCN: 一旦它指一段时辰，就能接 the whole of 这样的数量短语。

senses.title: The word in broadcasts
senses.definition: used in news and broadcasts to mark the report of the present day
senses.definitionCN: 新闻与广播中用来标明当天的报道
senses.example: Tonight we report on the election results from three regions.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚我们报道三个地区的选举结果。
senses.why: A broadcast must fix the day on which the listener hears it, so the word becomes a standard opening marker.
senses.whyCN: 广播必须钉住听众听到它的那一天，于是这个词成了标准的开场标记。

senses.title: An evening out
senses.definition: the evening's entertainment, especially when it is planned
senses.definitionCN: 今晚的娱乐活动，尤指事先安排好的
senses.example: Tonight is our anniversary dinner, so the whole family is coming.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚是我们的周年晚餐，全家人都来。
senses.why: In the phrase tonight is our dinner, the word stands in for the whole arrangement of the evening.
senses.whyCN: 在「今晚是我们的晚餐」这句话里，这个词代表整个晚上的安排。

senses.title: The coming night as a deadline
senses.definition: the present evening as the moment by which something must be done
senses.definitionCN: 把今晚当作某事必须完成的时刻
senses.example: The report has to be in tonight, or the printer will miss the morning edition.
senses.exampleCN: 报告今晚必须交，否则印刷厂会赶不上早报。
senses.why: Because the evening ends at midnight, the word can act as a deadline that is still ahead.
senses.whyCN: 因为夜晚到午夜就结束，这个词可以充当一个尚未到达的截止时刻。

senses.title: The word as a farewell
senses.definition: used in a farewell to mean that the speaker expects to meet again the same evening
senses.definitionCN: 道别时说，表示今晚还会再见
senses.example: See you tonight, she said, and closed the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她说了句今晚见，就把门关上了。
senses.why: A farewell can safely point at tonight because the same evening has still to happen.
senses.whyCN: 道别时可以放心指向今晚，因为这一晚还没发生。

intro.en: Tonight is a native compound of the preposition to and the noun night, built on the same model as today and tomorrow.
intro.cn: tonight 是介词 to 与名词 night 构成的本土复合词，其模式与 today、tomorrow 相同。

items.en: The phrase to niht, written as two words, means in or during this night.
items.cn: 古英语短语 to niht 写作两个词，意为今夜、在这夜里。

items.en: The two words begin to be written as one, toniht, and the sense narrows to the present evening.
items.cn: 两个词开始连写为 toniht，含义收窄为今晚。

items.en: The modern spelling tonight is fixed in the eighteenth century, at the same time as today takes its present form.
items.cn: 现代拼写 tonight 于十八世纪定型，与 today 定型的时间相同。

items.en: The noun use appears as soon as the compound is felt to be one word, as in the preparations for tonight.
items.cn: 一旦这个复合词被感觉成一个词，名词用法就出现了，如「为今晚做准备」。

items.en: Broadcasting gives the word a fixed function as a time marker at the start of reports.

definition_zh: 点头；点头示意；打盹；致意
definition_en: to move the head quickly down and up as a greeting or sign of agreement, and also to fall asleep briefly
core_image: 下巴向下一沉，又立刻弹回原位
scene: 散会后，他没有开口，只朝门口等着的同事低了下头，随即转身离开。 He gave her a brief nod and walked out of the room.
sceneCN: 这里 nod 是「点头示意」（第 1 个义项：以点头表示问候或同意）；句意为他朝她轻轻点了下头，就走出了房间。图中可辨识物件：半开的会议室门、走廊里的同事、手里的文件。

derivatives.zh: nod 加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「点头的；（花枝等）低垂的」
nod 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er，义为「点头的人」

senses.title: To move the head down and up as a greeting or sign of agreement
senses.definition: to move the head quickly down and up, especially to greet someone or to show that you agree
senses.definitionCN: 快速地把头低下再抬起，尤用于问候别人或表示同意
senses.example: She nodded when I asked whether she agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 我问她是否同意时，她点了点头。
senses.why: A nod is the smallest visible yes: the head dips and returns, and the whole body quietly accepts what has just been said.
senses.whyCN: 点头是最小的一个看得见的「是」：头低下去又回来，整个身体就安静地接受了刚才听到的话。

senses.title: To fall asleep briefly, especially when you should stay awake
senses.definition: to begin to sleep accidentally for a short time, often while sitting or listening
senses.definitionCN: 在不该睡的时候不小心睡着一小会儿，常发生在坐着或听讲时
senses.example: He nodded off during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 他在讲座中打起了瞌睡。
senses.why: The same drooping motion that signals sleepiness ends in a real loss of attention, so the verb stretches from a greeting to a head that falls forward and stays down.
senses.whyCN: 同一个耷拉下去的动作本是困意的信号，最后却变成真正的走神，于是词义从问候扩到「头垂下去、撑不住睡着」。

senses.title: A single quick movement of the head
senses.definition: a single quick movement of the head down and back up, used as a signal
senses.definitionCN: 头快速低下再抬起的一次动作，用作某种信号
senses.example: She answered with a quick nod.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻点了一下头作为回答。
senses.why: When the gesture is seen as an event rather than an act, the same word becomes a noun that counts each dip of the head.
senses.whyCN: 当这个手势被看成一件发生的事，而不是一个动作时，同一个词就变成名词，数得清每一次低头。

senses.title: An act of acknowledgement or tribute
senses.definition: a gesture, design or remark that openly acknowledges or honours someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示认可或致敬的动作、设计或言辞
senses.example: The new building is a nod to the town's fishing past.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新建筑是在向小镇的渔业历史致意。
senses.why: A small gesture of recognition is enough to say that something deserves respect, so the word widens from the head movement to any quiet sign of approval.
senses.whyCN: 一个很小的致意动作，就足以说明某样东西值得尊重；于是词义从头部的动作扩展到任何安静的认可。

intro.en: Nod is first recorded in Middle English, and its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally treated as an expressive gesture word rather than a borrowing from Latin.
intro.cn: nod 最早记录于中古英语，更早的来源不确定；一般认为它是模仿动作的表达性词语，而不是借自拉丁语。

items.en: The verb appears first in Middle English, and no reliable older root has been established; most dictionaries mark its origin as uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词最早出现在中古英语，没有可靠的更早词根被确认；多数词典都标注其来源不确定。

items.en: Nodden meant to make a quick bowing movement of the head, close to the modern gesture.
items.cn: nodden 意为把头快速低一下，和现代的手势已经很接近。

items.en: The word is attested in writing from the fourteenth century with the sense of the head movement.
items.cn: 这个词从十四世纪起见于书面记录，表示头部的这一动作。

items.en: The phrase nod off appears for falling asleep in a chair, adding the sleep sense to the family.
items.cn: nod off 这个说法出现，用于在椅子上睡着，为这个词族添上了「打盹」的义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb, uses the noun for the gesture, and extends a nod to to mean tribute.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动词，用名词指这个动作，并把 a nod to 扩展为致敬之意。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on nod, plus one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers other small signals and other words for light sleep.
note.cn: 形近组收由 nod 构成的形式，另收一个只是长得像的词；近义组收其他细小的示意动作，以及表示浅睡的词。

entries.definitionCN: nod 的现在分词兼形容词，也用于花枝低垂。

entries.definition: A person who nods, often repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 点头的人，常指反复点头的人。

entries.definitionCN: 「脑袋」的古老口语说法；只是拼写与 nod 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To bend the upper body forward as a greeting or sign of respect.

entries.definition: To signal to someone with a movement of the hand or head.
entries.definitionCN: 用手或头的动作示意某人过来。

entries.definition: To sleep lightly for a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 浅浅地睡一小会儿。

entries.definition: A short sleep, usually planned, during the day.
entries.definitionCN: 白天的小睡，通常是有意安排的。

normalIntro.en: The word is probably an expressive gesture word, and its family keeps circling small head movements, approval and sudden sleep.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很可能是模仿动作的表达性词语；词族始终围绕头部的细微动作、许可以及突然的睡意。

normal.en: A nod is one dip and return, unlike a bow, which bends the whole upper body.
normal.cn: 点头只是一次低头再抬起，与弯下整个上身的鞠躬不同。

normal.en: The past form doubled the final consonant: nod becomes nodded, not noded.
normal.cn: 过去式要双写词尾辅音：nod 变成 nodded，不是 noded。

normal.en: Nod off stretches the gesture into sleep, as if the head dips and never comes back.
normal.cn: nod off 把这个动作拖成了睡眠，好像头低下去就再没抬回来。

normal.en: Get the nod means to be approved or chosen, because approval was once given with a silent nod.
normal.cn: get the nod 表示获准或被选中，因为过去常以一个无声的点头表示同意。

normal.en: A nod to is figurative: the head gesture becomes a sign of respect for something old.
normal.cn: a nod to 是比喻用法：点头这个动作变成了对旧事物的尊重。

abstract.en: A gesture too small for words carries a complete yes, which is why nodding survives in every crowded room.
abstract.cn: 一个小到不需要言语的动作，却承载了完整的「是」，所以点头在每个拥挤的房间里都还活着。

abstract.en: The same downward motion marks both politeness and exhaustion, and the language keeps both in one word.
abstract.cn: 同一个向下的动作，既表示礼貌，也表示疲惫，而语言把它俩留在同一个词里。

abstract.en: Nod is the body answering before the mouth has decided what to say.
abstract.cn: nod 是身体在嘴巴想好说什么之前，先替它作了回答。

examples.cn: 我问她是否同意时，她点了点头。

examples.en: He nodded off during the lecture.
examples.cn: 他在讲座中打起了瞌睡。

examples.en: The director gave the young actor the nod.
examples.cn: 导演点头选中了那位年轻演员。

core_image: 指尖点着跳绳的次数，一二三四五
scene: 体育课测跳绳，同桌帮小芳记数。 She managed one hundred and two skips, counting every one.

senses.title: To say numbers in order
senses.definition: to say numbers one by one to find a total
senses.definitionCN: 逐一报数以求总数
senses.example: Let's count how many players are on the field.
senses.exampleCN: 我们数数场上有多少球员。
senses.why: The root means to reckon, moving item by item like steps.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是计算，像迈步一样逐项清点。

senses.title: To include or matter
senses.definition: to include someone or something; to be important
senses.definitionCN: 把某人某物计入；起重要作用
senses.example: Every point counts in the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛中每一分都很关键。
senses.why: What is counted is taken into the total, so counted things matter.
senses.whyCN: 被计入的进入总数，所以被计数之物重要。

senses.title: The act or total of counting
senses.definition: the action of finding a number, or the number found
senses.definitionCN: 计数的行为或所得的数字
senses.example: The count of the class vote was twenty-eight.
senses.exampleCN: 班级投票的计票结果是二十八票。
senses.why: The verb's work becomes a noun number.
senses.whyCN: 动词的成果化为名词数字。

senses.title: To rely on someone
senses.definition: to depend on or trust someone to help
senses.definitionCN: 信任并依赖某人
senses.example: You can count on me to bring the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 放心，球我来带。
senses.why: Counting someone in means their help is in your total.
senses.whyCN: 把某人算进来意味着其助力计入你的总数。

intro.en: Count came from Latin through French, from a word for reckoning.

items.en: The Latin verb computare meant to reckon or calculate, from com- (together) + putare (to think, reckon).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 computare 意为计算，由 com-（共同）+ putare（思考、估算）构成。

items.en: Old French counter meant to count or reckon.
items.cn: 古法语 counter 意为数、计算。

items.en: English adopted count in the fourteenth century.

items.en: The same French word named a noble, the count, keeper of accounts.
items.cn: 同一法语词还指掌管账目的贵族伯爵。

items.en: Modern uses spread to votes, ranks and even rhythm in music.

scene: 海浪不断拍打着岸边的岩石。 Waves kept beating against the rocks on the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 rock 是「岩石」（第 1 个义项：大块坚硬的石头）；句意：海浪不断拍打着岸边的岩石。

derivatives.zh: 多岩石的；摇晃的
摇椅；摇滚乐手

senses.title: A large stone
senses.definition: a large hard mass of stone
senses.definitionCN: 大块坚硬的石头
senses.example: A grey rock stood at the path's end.
senses.exampleCN: 小路尽头立着一块灰色岩石。
senses.why: The solid stone is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 坚实的石头是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Moving gently
senses.definition: to move gently from side to side
senses.definitionCN: 轻轻地左右移动
senses.example: She rocked the child to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻摇孩子入睡。
senses.why: The cradle repeats a slow side-to-side motion.
senses.whyCN: 摇篮重复着缓慢的左右摆动。

senses.title: Rock music
senses.definition: a loud popular music with strong beat
senses.definitionCN: 节奏强劲的响亮流行音乐
senses.example: The band plays old rock.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队演奏老摇滚。
senses.why: The music took the name of its rolling beat.
senses.whyCN: 这种音乐沿用了它翻滚般节奏的名字。

intro.en: Rock comes from Old French roche, from Medieval Latin rocca, a crag.
intro.cn: rock 源自古法语 roche，来自中世纪拉丁语 rocca（岩崖）。

items.en: Rocca means a crag or rock.
items.cn: rocca 意为岩崖或岩石。

items.en: Old French roche carries the stone sense.
items.cn: 古法语 roche 保留石头义。

items.en: Rock names stone, then a gentle sway.
items.cn: rock 先指石头，后指轻摇。

items.en: Rock music rises in the mid twentieth century.
items.cn: 摇滚乐在二十世纪中叶兴起。

items.en: Rock and roll links the sway and the sound.
items.cn: rock and roll 把摇摆与声音联系起来。

note.en: A rock is big and solid; a stone is smaller.
note.cn: rock 是大而坚实的石块，stone 通常更小。

entries.definition: full of rocks or unsteady
entries.definitionCN: 多岩石的；摇晃的

entries.definition: a rocking chair or rock musician
entries.definitionCN: 摇椅；摇滚乐手

entries.definition: moved gently
entries.definitionCN: 摇动过

entries.definition: a piece of hard rock
entries.definitionCN: 石头

entries.definition: a very large rock
entries.definitionCN: 巨石

entries.definition: to move slowly side to side
entries.definitionCN: 摇摆

normalIntro.en: Rock is stone, a sway, and a rolling beat.
normalIntro.cn: rock 既是石头，也是摇摆，还是一种翻滚的节奏。

normal.en: A large rock blocks the narrow path.
normal.cn: a large rock 堵住了狭窄的小路。

normal.en: Rock the baby gently in your arms.
normal.cn: rock the baby 就是在怀里轻轻摇晃婴儿。

normal.en: Rock climbing needs strong hands.
normal.cn: rock climbing 需要有力的双手。

normal.en: Solid rock is hard to dig through.
normal.cn: solid rock 很难挖穿。

normal.en: Rock music has a strong beat.
normal.cn: rock music 节奏强劲。

abstract.en: Picture waves striking a grey shore rock.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪拍打灰色的岸边岩石。

abstract.en: Imagine a cradle swinging in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静房间里摆动的摇篮。

abstract.en: Think of a stage shaking with a heavy beat.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台随沉重节拍震动。

examples.en: The boat hit a rock near the shore.
examples.cn: 小船在岸边撞上了岩石。

examples.en: He rocked the chair back and forth.
examples.cn: 他让椅子前后摇晃。

examples.en: They listened to rock all night.
examples.cn: 他们整夜听摇滚乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rock」听起来像「落磕」——从山上落下来磕人的硬块，就是岩石。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 rocca（岩崖）→ 古法语 roche → rock，核心义「坚硬的大石」，再由摇篮的摆动引申出摇动与摇滚乐。

sensesIntro.en: Rock means a large stone, a gentle swaying motion, or rock music.
sensesIntro.cn: rock 意为大块岩石、轻轻摇动，或摇滚乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey stone in moving waves.
core.cn: 核心意象：波浪中的灰色岩石。

branches.en: The stone is the oldest noun sense.
branches.cn: 石头是最古老的名词义项。

branches.en: The gentle sway is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 轻摇是动词义项。

branches.en: Rock music takes the rolling beat.
branches.cn: 摇滚乐沿用了翻滚的节拍。

branches.en: Even a heavy rock can rock in an earthquake.
branches.cn: 连沉重的岩石也会在地震中摇晃。

branches.en: The cradle sway and the music beat share motion.
branches.cn: 摇篮摆动与音乐节拍都共享运动感。

intro.en: Rock descends from Old French roche, a crag.
intro.cn: rock 源自古法语 roche（岩崖）。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin rocca is the earliest known form.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 rocca 是目前已知最早的形式。

items.example: Rocker names a chair or player.
The phrase joins sway and music.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把摇摆与音乐连在一起。

latinEntries.example: Rocca is the source of rock.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rocca 是 rock 的来源。

definition_zh: 打翻；弄翻；使心烦；使不适；（比赛）意外击败；心烦的；不快的
definition_en: to knock something over, to make someone unhappy, or to beat a stronger opponent unexpectedly
core_image: 手肘一碰，杯子朝桌上倒下去
scene: 婚礼前夜，有人把饮料碰洒在新娘的礼服上，所有人都慌了。 The news upset her so much that she could not sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 upset 是「使心烦」（第 2 个义项：让人心里翻腾不快）；句意为这个消息让她心烦得整夜没睡。手肘碰倒杯子的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 来自 distress 的过去分词，义为「痛苦的；忧虑的」
由 upset 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人不安的」

senses.title: To knock something over
senses.definition: to make a container or object fall over
senses.definitionCN: 使容器或物体倒下
senses.example: She upset the glass with her elbow.
senses.exampleCN: 她的手肘把杯子碰倒了。
senses.why: The word is up plus set: to set something up, or rather out of its place, until it falls over.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 up 加 set：把东西从原位「顶起来」，直到翻倒。

senses.title: To make someone unhappy
senses.definition: to make a person worried, hurt, or unhappy
senses.definitionCN: 使人担忧、难受或不快
senses.example: The letter upset him more than he showed.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让他心烦，比他表现出来的还要厉害。
senses.why: When a mind is knocked off balance like a cup, the person is upset, and the object becomes the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当心意像杯子一样被弄得失去平衡，人就成了 upset，物象便化为情绪。

senses.title: To disturb a plan or a system
senses.definition: to disturb an arrangement or a process
senses.definitionCN: 扰乱某个安排或进程
senses.example: The storm upset the whole timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨打乱了整个时刻表。
senses.why: A plan laid out like objects on a table can be knocked over too, and then nothing stays in place.
senses.whyCN: 摆好的计划就像桌上的物件，也可能被撞翻，之后便没有一样东西待在原位。

senses.title: To beat a stronger opponent
senses.definition: to defeat a team or player expected to win
senses.definitionCN: 击败被判为会赢的一方
senses.example: The visitors upset the champions in the final minute.
senses.exampleCN: 客队在最后一分钟爆冷赢下卫冕冠军。
senses.why: The result turns the table over: the side everyone placed first falls out of its place.
senses.whyCN: 这个结果把牌桌翻了过来：大家早先摆好的那一方从位子上跌落。

senses.title: A disturbed stomach
senses.definition: used of a stomach that feels unsettled
senses.definitionCN: 形容肚子不舒服、翻搅
senses.example: Too much fried food gives him an upset stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 油炸吃得太多，他就肠胃不适。
senses.why: Inside the body the same upsetting happens, and the stomach is described as turned over.
senses.whyCN: 身体内部也发生同样的翻搅，于是肠胃被说成「倒了」。

senses.title: A surprising defeat
senses.definition: a result in which the expected winner loses
senses.definitionCN: 本该获胜的一方却输了的结果
senses.example: The final was a real upset for the home crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛对主场观众来说是个大冷门。
senses.why: The noun keeps the picture of a table turned over, now applied to an expected result.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了桌面被翻掉的画面，只是这一次用在了原本意料之中的结果上。

intro.en: A two-part compound of native words whose first sense is physical and whose later senses are emotional.
intro.cn: 一个由本土词构成的两部分复合词，最初的意思是身体的，后来的意思是情绪的。

items.en: Up is an old adverb, and settan meant to place or put.
items.cn: up 是古副词，settan 意为「放置」。

items.en: Upsetten means to set up or to overturn, and the two meanings coexist.
items.cn: upsetten 兼有「竖起」与「推翻」两种意思，二者并存。

items.en: The sense of overturning settles first in the physical world of cups and carts.
items.cn: 「打翻」的意思先固定下来，用于杯子和推车这类实物。

items.en: By the eighteenth century upset describes a disturbed mind and a disturbed stomach.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，upset 已用于形容被搅乱的心情与肠胃。

items.en: The sports sense of an unexpected defeat appears in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「爆冷」这一体育含义在十九世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers up-set compounds and similar forms, while the near-meaning group collects words for troubling someone.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 up 与 set 组成的复合词及相近形式，近义组汇集表示使人难过的词。

normalIntro.en: A compound image that moves by easy steps from a falling cup to a troubled mind.
normalIntro.cn: 一个复合意象，从翻倒的杯子很自然地过渡到被搅乱的心。

normal.en: Up plus set: set it up so it tips over.
normal.cn: up 加 set：把东西顶起来直到翻倒。

normal.en: Be upset about something is the emotional frame learners need most.
normal.cn: be upset about 是学习者最需要的情绪框架。

normal.en: Upset is irregular: upset, upset, upset.
normal.cn: upset 的三态同形：upset、upset、upset。

normal.en: An upset stomach and a major upset show the two noun senses.
normal.cn: an upset stomach 与 a major upset 展示了两种名词义。

normal.en: Upsetting is the adjective for what causes the feeling.
normal.cn: upsetting 是表示「令人心烦」的形容词。

abstract.cn: 用手肘碰一下杯子，看它倒下。

abstract.en: See a chess board pushed an inch off the table.
abstract.cn: 看见棋盘被推离桌沿一点点。

abstract.en: Feel a plan come apart in the space of one phone call.
abstract.cn: 体会一个计划在一通电话里散架。

examples.en: Do not upset the tray when you leave the room.
examples.cn: 出房间时别把托盘碰翻。

examples.en: He was upset for days after the interview.
examples.cn: 面试之后他难受了好几天。

examples.en: The young team upset the favourites in the semi-final.
examples.cn: 这支年轻球队在半决赛爆冷击败了夺冠热门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆塞特」——阿婆塞东西太用力，一下把瓶罐塞翻在地，全家都慌了神。

sensesIntro.en: One tip-over spreads from cups to plans, to a person's mood, to a stomach, to a final score.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次翻倒，从杯子蔓延到计划、人的心情、肠胃，以至终场比分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup knocked over at the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上被碰倒的一只杯子。

branches.en: The object branch: a container goes down on its side.
branches.cn: 物件分支：容器倒向一边。

branches.en: The feeling branch: a mind knocked off its base.
branches.cn: 情绪分支：心意被撞离了底座。

branches.en: The order branch: arrangements turned over.
branches.cn: 秩序分支：安排被翻乱。

branches.en: The contest branch: the expected result is overturned.
branches.cn: 比赛分支：被认定会赢的结局被推翻。

definition_zh: 经理；管理者；球队或乐队的事务负责人；某项事务的专责人
definition_en: a person whose job is to organize and control the work of a business, team or activity
core_image: 缰绳从一只手伸向前方，前后都是一队等着被安排的人
scene: 演出前一天设备出了故障，那个人逐个打电话借音箱、改场地、重排时间。 A manager solves problems before the audience notices.
sceneCN: 这里 manager 指为一项活动统筹人、事与资源的人（第 1 个义项：负责机构或团队运转的人）；句意：一位经理在观众察觉之前就把问题解决掉。图中可辨识物件：音箱、改期通知、场地平面图、装设备的木箱。

pos.zh: 经理；管理者；事务负责人

derivatives.zh: 管理的；经理层的
经理职位
女经理（旧称）
管理；管理层

senses.title: The person who runs a business
senses.titleCN: 掌管一家企业或团队的人
senses.definition: a person employed to run a business, a team or a group of workers
senses.definitionCN: 受雇掌管一家企业、一支团队或一群工人的人
senses.example: The manager of the repair shop orders parts and sets the rota.
senses.exampleCN: 修理店的经理负责订零件、排班表。
senses.why: Manager is the noun of the hand that holds the rein, so it names whoever keeps the whole body of work moving.
senses.whyCN: manager 是握缰那只手的名词形式，指让全部工作继续转动的那个人。

senses.title: Head of one department
senses.definition: the person who heads a single department or function within a larger organization
senses.definitionCN: 在较大机构中主管某一个部门或职能的人
senses.example: The sales manager reports to the regional director.
senses.exampleCN: 销售经理向区域总监汇报。
senses.why: One department is a single rein of the firm, and its head pulls only that one.
senses.whyCN: 一个部门只是公司的一根缰绳，它的负责人只拉这一根。

senses.title: Boss of a sports team
senses.titleCN: 运动队的领队或主教练
senses.definition: the person who picks the players and directs a team during matches
senses.definitionCN: 挑选球员并在比赛中指挥球队的人
senses.example: The manager changed formation after the first goal.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个球之后，主教练换了阵型。
senses.why: The Italian verb behind the word was used of training horses, so a team boss keeps the oldest sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的意大利语动词用于驯马，因此球队主帅保留了最古老的那层意思。

senses.title: Business agent for performers
senses.titleCN: 艺人或乐队的事务代理人
senses.definition: someone who handles contracts, bookings and money for a performer or group
senses.definitionCN: 替艺人或团体处理合同、演出安排与收入的人
senses.example: Her manager turned down the film offer on her behalf.
senses.exampleCN: 她的经纪人替她推掉了那部电影的邀约。
senses.why: A performer needs someone to handle contracts the way a rider handles the direction of a horse.
senses.whyCN: 艺人需要有人替他打理合同，就像骑手替马把握方向。

senses.title: Someone who looks after another's money or property
senses.titleCN: 替他人打理钱财产业的人
senses.definition: a person employed to look after money, land or property for its owner
senses.definitionCN: 受雇替业主照管钱财、土地或房产的人
senses.example: The estate manager hires the gardeners and pays the bills.
senses.exampleCN: 产业经理雇请园丁，并支付各项账单。
senses.why: Money and land are things a hand holds on another's behalf, so the handler is named after the hand.
senses.whyCN: 钱财与土地是手替别人握着的东西，因此这个代管者以「手」来命名。

senses.title: A program that organizes things
senses.titleCN: 整理文件或窗口的计算机程序
senses.definition: a piece of software that organizes files, windows or settings
senses.definitionCN: 整理文件、窗口或设置的软件
senses.example: The download manager keeps the parts in order.
senses.exampleCN: 下载管理器把各个分段按顺序放好。
senses.why: Software does by rule what a hand did by feel: it keeps the pieces sorted in their places.
senses.whyCN: 软件用规则去做手凭手感做的事：把各个零碎归到各自的位置。

senses.title: The person in charge of one project
senses.titleCN: 某一项目的专责负责人
senses.definition: the person responsible for one project from start to finish
senses.definitionCN: 从头到尾对某一个项目负责的人
senses.example: The project manager moved the launch back by a month.
senses.exampleCN: 项目经理把上线日期往后推了一个月。
senses.why: A project is one bounded task, and its manager holds only that task until it is finished.
senses.whyCN: 一个项目是一项有边界的工作，项目经理只管这一件，直到它完成。

senses.title: The person in charge of a shop
senses.titleCN: 一家店铺的现场负责人
senses.definition: the person who runs a single shop or branch day to day
senses.definitionCN: 日复一日经营一家店铺或分店的人
senses.example: The store manager counts the till before locking up.
senses.exampleCN: 门店经理在锁门前清点收银账目。
senses.why: A shop is a small ring of work, and one person keeps that ring turning every day.
senses.whyCN: 一家店是一个小小的循环，一个人每天让它转起来。

intro.en: Manager adds the agent suffix to manage, a word that came from Italian horse handling. The role names grew apart as firms, clubs and estates each needed a handler.
intro.cn: manager 在 manage 之后加上施动后缀；manage 来自意大利语的驯马行话。随着公司、俱乐部与产业各自需要有人打理，这个称呼分化出不同角色。

items.en: Manus 'hand' also carried the idea of control, which is why a handler and a controller share one root.
items.cn: manus「手」同时带有掌控之意，因此「动手的人」与「掌控的人」共用同一个词根。

items.en: Maneggiare meant to handle and especially to train a horse; the trainer of horses is the oldest kind of manager.
items.cn: maneggiare 指用手操作，尤指驯马；驯马人就是最古老的一类管理者。

items.en: Manage is recorded in English from the sixteenth century, and manager, the one who manages, from the late sixteenth century; both dates are approximate.
items.cn: manage 在十六世纪见于英语记录，指做这件事的 manager 则见于十六世纪晚期；两个年代都是约数。

items.en: The Old English suffix -er marks the doer of an action, so manager is literally the handling one.
items.cn: 古英语的施动后缀标记动作的执行者，因此 manager 字面上就是「动手打理的那一个」。

items.en: Sports clubs, theatres and country estates gave the word its separate everyday roles in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: 体育俱乐部、剧院与乡间产业在十八、十九世纪分别赋予这个词不同的日常角色。

note.en: The first group shares shape or root with manager; the second group names other people who direct work.
note.cn: 第一组与 manager 共享形音或词根；第二组是其他指挥工作的人。

entries.definition: The verb, naming the action rather than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指动作而不是人。

entries.definition: The activity or the whole body of managers, not one individual.
entries.definitionCN: 指这项活动或整个管理层，不是单个个人。

entries.definition: A riding school, from the same Italian word for handling horses.
entries.definitionCN: 马术学校，同出那个表示驯马的意大利词。

entries.definition: From Dutch manneken 'little man'; the shared shape is accidental, and it names a dummy.
entries.definitionCN: 来自荷兰语 manneken「小人」；形似只是巧合，它指服装模特或假人。

entries.definition: One who watches over workers directly; the emphasis is on checking, not on running the whole unit.
entries.definitionCN: 直接看管工人的人，强调检查，而不是经营整个单元。

entries.definition: One who runs an institution's procedures and records; the focus is rules and paper.
entries.definitionCN: 维持机构程序与记录的人，重心在规章与文书。

entries.definition: A member of the top board or the head of a whole organization.
entries.definitionCN: 董事会成员或整个机构的负责人。

entries.definition: An informal word for whoever gives orders; it says nothing about handling work well.
entries.definitionCN: 指发号施令者的口语词，并不含「把工作打理得好」的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real word family and real job titles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的同族词与真实的职位名称。

normal.en: Manus is hand, and -er is the doer, so manager is the one with a hand on the work.
normal.cn: manus 是手，施动后缀指做事的人，manager 就是那只按在工作上的手。

normal.en: The family runs manage, management, managerial and managership.
normal.cn: 同族词有 manage、management、managerial 与 managership。

normal.en: Real titles show the spread: store manager, project manager, sales manager.
normal.cn: 真实职位显示它的分布：门店经理、项目经理、销售经理。

normal.en: The oldest picture is a horse trainer, because the Italian verb meant exactly that.
normal.cn: 最古老的画面是驯马人，因为那个意大利语动词本就是这个意思。

normal.en: A manager is measured by the work that keeps moving, not by tasks done personally.
normal.cn: 衡量一位经理的，是继续运转的工作，而不是他亲手做完的活儿。

abstract.en: Picture a stagehand who fixes a broken light while the curtain is still closed.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布还没拉开，一名舞台工作人员已经把坏掉的灯修好。

abstract.en: Picture a rider who steers with the knees and leaves both hands free.
abstract.cn: 想象一位用膝盖控向、腾出双手的骑手。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing at the joint of four pipes, turning each valve a little.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在四根管道的接合处，把每个阀门都拧一点。

examples.en: The branch manager rewrote the rota so nobody worked six days straight.
examples.cn: 分店经理重排了班表，没人再连上六天。

examples.en: A good manager knows which decisions can wait until Monday.
examples.cn: 好的管理者知道哪些决定可以等到周一再做。

examples.en: The band's manager cancelled the tour rather than cut the fee.
examples.cn: 乐队经纪人宁可取消巡演，也不肯压低酬劳。

root: 拉丁 manus「手」→ 意大利 maneggiare「驯马、操作」→ 英语 manage「管理」+ 施动后缀「做事的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hand from a whole firm down to a single shop: the general runner, a department head, a team boss, an agent for another, a keeper of property, a sorting program, one project and one counter.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一只手，从整个公司缩小到一家店铺：总管、部门负责人、球队主帅、代他人打理事务者、产业代管人、整理文件的程序、单个项目、一个柜台。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand on the rein, with a line of people and tasks behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握着缰绳，身后是一队人与一列待办的事。

branches.en: THE WHOLE REIN: the general manager holds every part of the business at once.
branches.cn: 整根缰绳：总经理同时握住企业的每一部分。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF CAPTAIN: one leads a department, the other leads players.
branches.cn: 两种带队人：一个带部门，一个带球员。

branches.en: ACTING FOR ANOTHER: an agent handles a career, an estate manager handles property.
branches.cn: 代他人出手：经纪人打理职业生涯，产业经理打理房产。

branches.en: ORGANIZING INSTRUMENTS: software sorts files, a project lead sorts tasks.
branches.cn: 整理的工具：软件归置文件，项目负责人归置任务。

branches.en: ONE SMALL RING: a single shop is the smallest circle a manager keeps turning.
branches.cn: 最小的循环：一家店铺是经理让它转动的最小一圈。

intro.en: Manager is a Latin-rooted verb plus an English agent suffix, and the same root reaches several everyday words.
intro.cn: manager 是一个拉丁词根的动词加上英语施动后缀，这个词根还通向若干日常词。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus gives manual, manacle and mandate; the Italian verb gives manage and its English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 manus 衍生 manual、manacle 与 mandate；意大利语动词衍生 manage 及其英语词族。

definition_zh: 在中途；到一半；半路； halfway house 过渡站
definition_en: at the middle point between two places or stages; partly done
core_image: 徒步者在两座山之间的歇脚亭里坐下，前不着村后不着店
scene: 长跑测试中，学生们绕操场跑到第二个弯道就到了半程点。 We stopped halfway through the race for a drink of water.
sceneCN: 这里 halfway 是「在中途」（第 1 个义项：位于两地或两阶段的中点）；句意是赛跑进行到一半时我们停下喝水。

derivatives.zh: halfway 的基础词，义为「一半」
同族合成词，义为「半心半意的」

senses.title: At the middle of a route
senses.definition: at the point equally distant from the start and the end
senses.definitionCN: 位于起点与终点距离相等的那一点
senses.example: The bus stopped halfway up the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在半山腰停了下来。
senses.why: The rest shelter sits where effort equals remaining effort, the natural midpoint.
senses.whyCN: 歇脚亭所在之处，已走的路与将走的路恰好相等，这就是天然中点。

senses.title: At the middle of an activity
senses.definition: partly through an event, task, or period of time
senses.definitionCN: 活动、任务或时段进行了一部分
senses.example: Halfway through the film the power went out.
senses.exampleCN: 电影放到一半停电了。
senses.why: Any process is a road in disguise, so its middle borrows the travel word.
senses.whyCN: 一切过程都是变相的道路，其中点自然借用旅途词汇。

senses.title: Partly done or achieved
senses.definition: not finished; only partly complete
senses.definitionCN: 尚未完成；只完成了一部分
senses.example: The bridge is only halfway built.
senses.exampleCN: 大桥只建了一半。
senses.why: A stalled task stands frozen at its middle point, half a road behind it.
senses.whyCN: 搁浅的任务停在自己中点上，身后只有半条路。

senses.title: A compromise position
senses.definition: agreeing by each side giving up part of a demand
senses.definitionCN: 双方各让一步达成的中间立场
senses.example: Let us meet halfway on the price.
senses.exampleCN: 价格上我们各让一步吧。
senses.why: Two people walking toward each other meet at the middle, so deals use the same point.
senses.whyCN: 两人相向而行必在中点相遇，谈判也借用同一位置。

senses.title: Halfhearted or lukewarm
senses.definition: showing only partial effort, support, or warmth
senses.definitionCN: 只投入部分努力、支持或热情
senses.example: His halfway apology satisfied nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 他不冷不热的道歉谁也不满意。
senses.why: A compromise spirit can shrink to a personality trait, lukewarm and unconvincing.
senses.whyCN: 折中的姿态缩小为性格特质，便成了温吞无力的敷衍。

intro.en: Halfway is simply half on a road, and its history mirrors the mother word.
intro.cn: halfway 就是「路上的半个」，历史与母词 half 如出一辙。

items.en: Old English healf carried the side-of-a-cut idea.
items.cn: 古英语 healf 承载「一刀之侧」的概念。

items.en: Old English weg meant road or way, a daily travel word.
items.cn: 古英语 weg 意为道路，是日常出行用词。

items.en: Middle English joined them as half way, first for physical midpoints.
items.cn: 中古英语把两词合并为 half way，最初指实际的中点。

items.en: The compound later stretched to time and progress midpoints.
items.cn: 合成词随后延伸到时间与进程的中点。

items.en: Modern English solidified the one-word spelling and the compromise senses.
items.cn: 现代英语固化了单词拼写与折中义项。

note.en: Words near halfway in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 halfway 形近或义近的词。

examples.en: The climbers rested halfway up the peak.

definition_zh: 添加；增加；相加；补充说
definition_en: to put something together with another thing, or to join numbers
core_image: 把牛奶倒进面粉里
scene: 厨房里，妈妈把牛奶倒进面粉里。 She added milk to the flour.
sceneCN: 这里 added 是「添加」（第 1 个义项：把一物加到另一物里）；句意为她把牛奶加进面粉里。

senses.title: To put one thing with another
senses.definition: to put something together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 把某物与另一物放在一起
senses.example: Add some sugar to the tea.
senses.exampleCN: 往茶里加些糖。
senses.why: Add comes from Latin addere, to give to, so the first picture is giving one thing to another.
senses.whyCN: add 来自拉丁语 addere「给到」，最初的画面就是把一物给到另一物上。

senses.title: To join numbers
senses.definition: to join numbers to find a total
senses.definitionCN: 把数字合起来求出总数
senses.example: If you add three and four, you get seven.
senses.exampleCN: 三加四等于七。
senses.why: Numbers are treated like a pile, and joining them is adding one amount to another.
senses.whyCN: 数目被看成一堆东西，把两堆合起来就是相加。

senses.title: To say more
senses.definition: to say something more after what was said
senses.definitionCN: 在已说过的话之后再补充
senses.example: She added that the shop was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 她补充说商店关门了。
senses.why: Words are also added: a further remark is put after the first one.
senses.whyCN: 话也可以被「加上」：在原先的话后面再放一句，就是补充说。

senses.title: To make a quality stronger
senses.definition: to put in something that increases a quality
senses.definitionCN: 加入某物使某种性质增强
senses.example: A lamp added warmth to the room.
senses.exampleCN: 一盏灯给房间增添了温暖。
senses.why: A quality can be increased by putting something into the scene, as a lamp adds warmth.
senses.whyCN: 把某物放进环境里让某种性质变强，就是增添。
