definition_zh: 听；倾听；听从；留心等着听；偷听
definition_en: to give deliberate attention to sound, to heed what is said, to wait for a particular sound, or to overhear a conversation
core_image: 一个人停下手里的活，侧耳朝向声音来源
scene: 夜里屋子很静，母亲关掉电视，侧耳对着楼上婴儿床的方向。 She turned down the radio and listened for the baby's cry.
sceneCN: 这里 listen 是「留心等着听」（第 3 个义项：等某个声音出现）；句意为她调低收音机，等着听婴儿的哭声。画面里可抓住的物件：关掉的电视、楼上的婴儿床、调低的音量。

pos.zh: 听；倾听；听从；留心等着听；偷听

derivatives.zh: 由 listen 加 -er 构成，指听的人，尤指收听节目的听众
由 listen 加 -ing 构成，指听的行为，也指用心倾听的
由 listen 加 -able 构成，指听着不难受、值得一听的

senses.title: To give attention to sound
senses.titleCN: 听：把注意力放到声音上
senses.definition: to give deliberate attention to a sound or to someone speaking
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地把注意力放在某个声音或某人的说话上
senses.example: She listened to the rain on the roof until she fell asleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她听着屋顶上的雨声，直到睡着。
senses.why: Old English had hlysnan for attending to sound beside hyran for simply hearing; the two verbs split the work, and listen took the side of effort and attention rather than passive reception.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里 hlysnan 表示注意地听，hyran 表示听见；两个动词分工，listen 占了「费心去听」这一边，而不是被动接收。

senses.title: To heed advice or a warning
senses.titleCN: 听从：把听到的话当回事
senses.definition: to pay attention to advice, a warning, or a request and act on it
senses.definitionCN: 重视劝告、警告或请求并照着去做
senses.example: He never listens to his doctor about sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不听医生关于睡眠的建议。
senses.why: Hearing turns into obedience when the listener acts on what was said; the same verb slides from the ear to behaviour, which is why listen to reason and listen to your parents sound natural.
senses.whyCN: 当听的人照着话去做，听见就变成了服从；同一个动词从耳朵滑到行为，所以 listen to reason（听劝）和听父母的话都很自然。

senses.title: To wait and watch for a particular sound
senses.titleCN: 留心等着听：等某个声音出现
senses.definition: to keep one's attention on the possibility of a particular sound, especially in order to respond
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力放在某个可能出现的声响上，以便及时反应
senses.example: The guard listened for footsteps on the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 守卫留神听着楼梯上的脚步声。
senses.why: The preposition for turns listening into a search: nothing has been heard yet, and the ear is held open for a signal, as in listen for the doorbell.
senses.whyCN: 介词 for 把「听」变成「找」：此刻还没有声音，只是把耳朵开着等一个信号，如留神听门铃。

senses.title: To overhear others on purpose
senses.titleCN: 偷听：躲在暗处听别人说话
senses.definition: to hear a conversation that is not meant for you, often by staying hidden or by using a device
senses.definitionCN: 听到并非说给自己听的谈话，常靠躲藏或借助设备
senses.example: Someone was listening in on the meeting from the next room.
senses.exampleCN: 有人躲在隔壁房间偷听会议。
senses.why: The particle in adds the idea of entering a space that is not yours, so listen in on marks the listener as an outsider who was never invited.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 in 加进「进入不属于自己的空间」的意思，所以 listen in on 把听者标成未被邀请的外人。

intro.en: Listen goes back to a Germanic verb for hearing with attention; the h of its Old English form was later dropped, and the word is widely linked to the root behind loud.
intro.cn: listen 源自日耳曼语中表示「用心听」的动词；古英语形式里的 h 后来被丢掉，一般认为它与 loud 同源。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ḱlew- meant to hear, and it also underlies words for fame, since being heard of is being talked about.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ḱlew- 意为「听见」，也衍生出表示名声的词，因为被人听说就是被人谈论。

items.en: *hlusinōn, a verb of listening, grew beside *hlūdaz, the adjective that became loud; both point back to the act of hearing.
items.cn: *hlusinōn 是表示「听」的动词，与后来变成 loud 的形容词 *hlūdaz 并生；两者都指向「听见」这一行为。

items.en: Old English wrote the verb as hlysnan, with an h that speakers later stopped pronouncing.
items.cn: 古英语把动词写作 hlysnan，词首的 h 后来在口语中不再发音。

items.en: Middle English settled on listen, dropped the h in spelling, and kept the meaning of giving ear to something.
items.cn: 中古英语定型为 listen，拼写中去掉 h，保留「把耳朵给某物」的意思。

items.en: Modern English adds listener and listening, and the phrasal forms listen in and listen up, which push the word toward eavesdropping and toward a call for attention.
items.cn: 现代英语派生 listener 与 listening，并发展出 listen in、listen up 等短语，把词义推向偷听与提醒注意。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built with listen; the near-meaning group separates deliberate listening from mere hearing and from related acts of attention.
note.cn: 形近组收由 listen 构成的词形；近义组把刻意的「听」与单纯的「听见」以及相关的注意行为区分开。

entries.definition: A person who listens, especially to a radio programme.
entries.definitionCN: 听的人；收听节目的听众。

entries.definition: The act of paying attention to sound, or an adjective for such activity.

entries.definition: To listen secretly to a private conversation.

normalIntro.en: The word is carried by an Old English verb, its lost h, a Germanic root shared with loud, and English endings that make a listener and a listening.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由古英语动词、失落了的 h、与 loud 共有的日耳曼词根，以及构成 listener 与 listening 的英语词尾共同支撑。

normal.en: Old English wrote the verb with an h, so the silent letter in today's spelling is a leftover, not a rule about pronunciation.
normal.cn: 古英语写法带 h，所以今天拼写里的不发音字母是遗留物，并不是发音规则。

normal.en: Listener is listen plus -er, the person at the receiving end of the sound.
normal.cn: listener 是 listen 加 -er，指声音接收端的那个人。

normal.en: Hear is what happens to you; listen is what you decide to do, and English keeps both verbs.
normal.cn: hear 是发生在你身上的事，listen 是你决定去做的事，英语把两个动词都保留下来。

normal.en: Listen for waits for a signal; listen to receives what is already there; the preposition marks the difference.
normal.cn: listen for 是等一个信号，listen to 是接收已经在那里的声音，介词标出了这个差别。

normal.en: Listen in on adds in because the listener steps into a space where he was not invited.
normal.cn: listen in on 之所以加 in，是因为听者走进了没有邀请他的空间。

abstract.en: To listen is to lend someone your ears for a while, which is why the verb so easily turns into obedience.
abstract.cn: 倾听是把耳朵借给别人一段时间，所以这个动词很容易变成服从。

abstract.en: Attention has a direction: you can listen to, listen for, or listen in, and each preposition draws a different boundary.
abstract.cn: 注意力是有方向的：可以 listen to、listen for、listen in，每个介词都画出不同的边界。

abstract.en: A word for hearing can grow into a word for trust, because people who are heard are also more likely to be followed.
abstract.cn: 表示「听」的词能长成表示「信任」的词，因为被听见的人也更容易被跟随。

examples.cn: 她听着雨声直到睡着。

examples.en: The guard listened for footsteps on the stairs.

examples.en: He never listens to his doctor.
examples.cn: 他从不听医生的劝。

definition_zh: 银行；岸；堤；一排；存钱；指望
definition_en: a business that keeps and lends money, or the land along the side of a river
core_image: 河岸的斜坡上长着草，水面在下面缓缓流过
scene: 河岸边长满高高的芦苇，孩子们坐在岸边钓鱼。 They sat on the bank of the river and fished all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 bank 是「河岸」（第 2 个义项：河流旁边的陆地）；句意为他们坐在河岸上钓了一下午鱼。

derivatives.zh: 由 bank 加 -er 构成，义为「银行家」
由 bank 加 -ing 构成，义为「银行业务」
由 bank 与 note 组合而成，义为「纸币」
由 river 与 bank 组合而成，义为「河岸」

senses.title: A financial institution
senses.definition: a business that keeps money for people, lends money, and exchanges currency
senses.definitionCN: 替人保管钱、放贷并兑换货币的机构
senses.example: She went to the bank to open an account.
senses.exampleCN: 她去银行开了一个账户。
senses.why: Italian bankers worked at a bench or table, and the bench gave its name to the place that kept money.
senses.whyCN: 意大利的银行家在长凳或柜台前做生意，这条长凳的名字就成了保管钱财之地的名称。

senses.title: The land beside a river
senses.definition: the raised ground along the side of a river, lake, or canal
senses.definitionCN: 河流、湖泊或运河旁边隆起的土地
senses.example: They sat on the bank of the river and fished.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐在河岸上钓鱼。
senses.why: The land sense comes from a different old word for a ridge or shelf, which describes the raised edge of a river.
senses.whyCN: 「岸」义来自另一个表示「隆起、台架」的古词，正好描述河边隆起的地形。

senses.title: A row or pile
senses.definition: a long row or a mass of things placed side by side, such as clouds or machines
senses.definitionCN: 并排摆放的一长排或一大堆东西，如云或机器
senses.example: A bank of clouds covered the western sky.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆云遮住了西边的天空。
senses.why: A raised ridge looks like a long heap, so any long heap or row takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 隆起的埂看起来像长长的一堆，于是任何长排或长堆都叫这个名字。

senses.title: To keep money in a bank
senses.definition: to put money into a bank account
senses.definitionCN: 把钱存进银行账户
senses.example: He banks half of his pay every month.
senses.exampleCN: 他每月把一半工资存进银行。
senses.why: The verb turns the institution into an action: sending money to the place that keeps it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把机构变成动作：把钱送到保管它的地方。

senses.title: To depend on
senses.definition: in the phrase bank on, to depend on something happening
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 bank on，指指望某事发生
senses.example: You can bank on her to arrive on time.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以指望她准时到。
senses.why: Money placed in a bank is trusted to be safe, so to bank on something is to trust it like a deposit.
senses.whyCN: 存进银行的钱被认为安全可靠，所以 bank on 某事就像把钱存进去那样信任它。

intro.en: Bank has two histories that happen to meet in one spelling: the money word came through Italian and French, the land word from Norse.
intro.cn: bank 有两条恰好汇成一个拼写的历史：表示钱财的词经意大利语与法语而来，表示陆地的词来自诺尔斯语。

items.en: A Germanic word for a shelf or bench lies behind the money sense and is related to the ridge sense.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示「台架、长凳」的词是「银行」义的远源，与「隆起」义也有联系。

items.en: Italian banca meant a money-changer's bench or table, and from the table came the business.
items.cn: 意大利语 banca 指钱币兑换商的长凳或桌子，生意就从这张桌子得名。

items.en: French banque carried the financial word into English.
items.cn: 法语 banque 把这个财务词带入英语。

items.en: Old Norse bakki meant a ridge or the raised land beside a river, which gives the land sense.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 bakki 指隆起的埂或河边的陆地，这就是「岸」义的来源。

items.en: The two senses now live side by side, and bank on extends the money image to trust and reliance.
items.cn: 两个义项现在并存，bank on 又把「钱」的意象扩展到信任与依靠。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the bank family and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers financial places, shores, and rows.
note.cn: 形近组收 bank 词族与复合词；近义组收金融机构、岸边与成排之物。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「河岸」，由 river 与 bank 组合而成。

entries.definition: The land along the edge of a sea or lake; wider than a river bank.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海岸、湖岸」，范围比河岸更宽。

entries.definition: The land next to the sea, seen as a whole line.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海岸」，指靠海的一整条陆地。

entries.definition: A line of things placed side by side; it matches the third sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一排」，对应第三个义项。

entries.definition: To put money into an account; the formal verb for the fourth sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「存入」，是第四个义项的正式说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Italian bench image, the Norse ridge image, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的意大利语「长凳」意象、诺尔斯语「隆起」意象，以及这个词的常见搭配。

normal.en: Italian bankers worked at a bench called banca, so the bench became the bank.
normal.cn: 意大利银行家在叫作 banca 的长凳上做生意，长凳就成了「银行」。

normal.en: The river bank is a raised ridge of land, which is why a bank can also mean a heap.
normal.cn: 河岸是隆起的土埂，所以 bank 也能表示一堆东西。

normal.en: Bank account and bank money keep the financial sense in daily use.
normal.cn: bank account 与 bank money 让财务义留在日常使用中。

normal.en: A blood bank stores blood the way a money bank stores money.
normal.cn: 血库像银行存钱一样存放血液。

normal.en: Bank on someone means trusting that person like a safe deposit.
normal.cn: bank on 某人，就是像信任一笔安全存款那样信任他。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden bench in a market: coins are counted on it, and the bench slowly turns into an institution.
abstract.cn: 想象集市上一张木长凳：钱币在上面被清点，这张长凳慢慢变成了一所机构。

abstract.en: The same word also pictures a green slope above water, because both are raised edges people stand on.
abstract.cn: 同一个词还画出一条水上的绿色斜坡，因为两者都是人站立的隆起边缘。

abstract.en: Money and river never meet in the real world, yet English keeps them in one word because both are edges that hold something.
abstract.cn: 现实里钱与河并不相遇，英语却让它们共用一个词，因为两者都是「兜住东西的边缘」。

examples.en: They sat on the bank of the river and fished all afternoon.
examples.cn: 他们坐在河岸上钓了一下午鱼。

examples.en: She went to the bank to open an account.
examples.cn: 她去银行开了一个账户。

examples.en: You can bank on her to arrive on time.
examples.cn: 你可以指望她准时到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「办卡」——去银行办卡存钱，出门就是河岸：银行、岸

root: 表示「银行」的 bank 经法语来自意大利语 banca「钱币兑换商的长凳」，可上溯到日耳曼语表示「台架、长凳」的词；表示「岸」的 bank 来自古诺尔斯语 bakki「隆起、河边陆地」。两条来源不同，现代同形。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of bank come from two old images that share one spelling: a bench where money is handled, and a raised edge of land, which also gives the row and the verb senses.
sensesIntro.cn: bank 的五个义项来自两个共用同一拼写的古老意象：处理钱币的长凳，以及隆起的土地边缘；后者又生出「一排」与动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low grassy slope rises above a river, while a wooden bench stands in a market.
core.cn: 核心意象：河面上方隆起一道长草的斜坡，集市上则摆着一张木长凳。

branches.en: THE BENCH: the money-changer's table becomes the institution that keeps money.
branches.cn: 长凳线：钱币兑换商的桌子变成了保管钱财的机构。

branches.en: THE RIDGE: the raised land beside a river is the second, separate origin.
branches.cn: 隆起线：河边隆起的土地是第二条独立来源。

branches.en: THE ROW: any long heap or line resembles that raised ridge.
branches.cn: 长排线：任何长堆或长排都像那道隆起的埂。

branches.en: THE DEPOSIT: the verb sends money to the bench that keeps it.
branches.cn: 存款线：动词把钱送到那张保管它的「长凳」上。

branches.en: THE TRUST: money kept safely becomes a model for relying on a person.
branches.cn: 信任线：被安全保管的钱，成了信任某个人的模型。

intro.en: Bank is a borrowed root with two histories; English expands it with -er, -ing and familiar compounds.
intro.cn: bank 是有两条来源的借入词根，英语用 -er、-ing 和常见复合词扩展它。

latinIntro.en: The financial sense passed through Italian banca, but that word is Germanic in origin, so no true Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 财务义经意大利语 banca 传来，但那个词本身源于日耳曼语，因此不列真正的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a money house or a river edge

items.exampleCN: 它与 bank 构成 banknote。
它与 bank 构成 riverbank。
它与 bank 构成 blood bank。
它与 bank 构成 bank on。

definition_zh: 准备；预备；使做好准备；配制；编写；筹备
definition_en: to make someone or something ready for what will happen, to put a dish or mixture together, or to draw up a plan or text
core_image: 案板上一排切好的菜，锅已烧热，手正把盐罐拉到近前
scene: 天还没亮，厨房的灯先亮了，她把米淘好放进锅里。 She prepared a simple breakfast before the children woke.
sceneCN: 这里 prepare 是「配制、做好（饭菜）」（第 2 个义项：把食材做成可以吃的东西）；句意为她在孩子们醒来之前做好了一顿简单的早饭。图中可辨识物件：案板、切好的菜、热锅、盐罐。

pos.zh: 准备；预备；使做好准备；配制；编写

derivatives.zh: 由 prepare 换用名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「准备；准备工作」
由拉丁词干 preparat- 加 -ory 构成，义为「预备的；筹备的」
由 prepare 加 -ed 构成，义为「有准备的；事先做好的」
由 prepared 加 -ness 构成，义为「有准备的状态；戒备」

senses.title: To get ready before something happens
senses.definition: to make yourself or something else ready for an event that is still to come
senses.definitionCN: 让自己或别的事物为尚未到来的事情进入就绪状态
senses.example: The team spent the morning preparing for the match.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍花了一上午为比赛做准备。
senses.why: Latin parare meant to make ready, and prae- adds the idea of doing it beforehand, so preparation is readiness produced in advance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 parare 意为使就绪，prae- 又加上「事先」的意思，所以 preparation 就是提前造出来的就绪状态。

senses.title: To put a dish or mixture together
senses.definition: to combine ingredients and make them ready to eat or to use
senses.definitionCN: 把各种材料组合起来，做成可以吃或可以用的东西
senses.example: He prepared a pot of soup for the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他为客人煮了一锅汤。
senses.why: Making a dish ready is the same act of putting things in order, so the verb moves from readiness in general to the kitchen without changing its core.
senses.whyCN: 把一道菜弄好，仍然是同样的「把东西整理到位」的动作，所以这个词从一般的就绪转到厨房，核心并没有变。

senses.title: To train or equip someone for a task
senses.definition: to give a person the knowledge or experience needed for a future task
senses.definitionCN: 让某人为将来的任务获得所需的知识或经验
senses.example: The course prepares students for work in a real lab.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课让学生为在真实实验室里工作做好准备。
senses.why: When the object is a person, readiness becomes training, and the verb names what teaching does before the test of real work.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是人时，就绪就变成了训练，这个词命名的正是教学在真实工作检验之前所做的那一步。

senses.title: To draw up a text or plan
senses.definition: to write or compose a document, plan or set of figures in advance
senses.definitionCN: 提前写出或编写成文件、方案或一组数字
senses.example: She prepared a short report for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她为会议写了一份简短报告。
senses.why: A document is also made ready before it is used, which is why the verb covers drawing up papers as well as cooking.
senses.whyCN: 文件在使用之前同样要先被弄好，所以这个词既能指做饭，也能指起草文书。

intro.en: Prepare is a Latin verb of making ready with a prefix meaning beforehand, filtered through Old French, and English widened it to meals, lessons, reports and medicine.
intro.cn: prepare 是一个加上「事先」前缀的拉丁「使就绪」动词，经古法语传入，英语又把它扩展到饭菜、功课、报告与药物。

items.en: Parare meant to make ready, to furnish or to put something in order; its deeper origin is uncertain and is usually left open.
items.cn: parare 意为使就绪、置办或把东西整理好；它更早的来源不确定，一般认为难以定论。

items.en: Prae- means before, so praeparare meant to get something ready ahead of the moment it would be needed.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在……之前」，praeparare 便指在需要之前就把事情弄好。

items.en: The participle praeparatus, made ready, supplied adjective and noun forms that later languages reused.
items.cn: 分词 praeparatus 意为「已备好的」，后来的语言沿用了它提供的形容词与名词形式。

items.en: Old French kept the verb as preparer, and English borrowed it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词保留为 preparer，英语在中世纪将其借入。

items.en: Modern English widened prepare to meals, lessons, reports and medicine, all sharing the idea of readiness made in advance.
items.cn: 现代英语把 prepare 扩展到饭菜、功课、报告与药物，这些用法共享「提前备好」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same Latin verb of readiness; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for getting things and people into position.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「使就绪」动词的形式；近义组收表示把事物与人安排到位的动词。

entries.definition: The act or process of getting ready, or a substance made ready for use.
entries.definitionCN: 由 prepare 转成的名词，指准备的过程，或配好的制剂。

entries.definition: Serving to get something ready, as in a preparatory course.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的形容词，义为预备的，如预科课程。

entries.definition: Ready, or made in advance rather than at the moment.
entries.definitionCN: 由 prepare 加 -ed 构成，义为有准备的、事先做好的。

entries.definition: To mend something; it comes from re- plus parare, to make ready again, so the root is shared but the meaning has moved.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的另一支，由 re- 加 parare（重新弄好）构成，词根相同但词义已转向修理。

entries.definition: To make something or someone completely prepared, used mostly in technical and military writing.
entries.definitionCN: 使完全就绪；多用于技术与军事文字。

entries.definition: To put things in a particular order or make plans for them.
entries.definitionCN: 安排；把事物按某种次序放好或作出计划。

entries.definition: To plan and put the parts of an activity into working order.
entries.definitionCN: 组织；把一项活动的各部分计划并安排妥当。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of readiness with a prefix of time, and its family keeps returning to what is done before the moment of use.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是带时间前缀的拉丁「使就绪」动词，同族词反复回到「在使用之前先做好」这件事。

normal.en: Parare means to make ready, and prae- adds before, so prepare is literally to ready something beforehand.
normal.cn: parare 意为使就绪，prae- 加上「之前」，所以 prepare 字面上就是提前把某事弄好。

normal.en: Preparation is the noun from the same stem, naming the whole process rather than the single act.
normal.cn: preparation 是同一词干的名词，指整个过程，而不只是单个动作。

normal.en: Prepared can be an adjective, which is why we say someone is well prepared.
normal.cn: prepared 也可以作形容词，所以可以说某人有充分准备。

normal.en: Repair shares the same parare but with re-, to make ready again, and has drifted to mending.
normal.cn: repair 同样用 parare，但带 re-（重新弄好），词义已漂移到修理。

normal.en: Prepare a meal and prepare a report both mean putting parts in order before they are needed.
normal.cn: prepare a meal 与 prepare a report 都指在需要之前把各部分整理到位。

abstract.en: To prepare is to work in the present on behalf of a moment that has not arrived.
abstract.cn: 准备就是在当下为尚未到来的时刻做事。

abstract.en: The word assumes the future will ask something of you, and it answers before the question is spoken.
abstract.cn: 这个词假定未来会向你提出要求，并在问题说出口之前就先作答。

abstract.en: Cooking, teaching and writing all appear under one verb because all three are ways of arranging the world in advance.
abstract.cn: 做饭、教学与写作都归到同一个动词下，因为三者都是提前把世界安排好的方式。

examples.en: She prepared a simple breakfast before the children woke.
examples.cn: 她在孩子们醒来之前做好了一顿简单的早饭。

examples.en: The team spent the morning preparing for the match.
examples.cn: 队伍花了一上午为比赛做准备。

examples.en: The course prepares students for work in a real lab.
examples.cn: 这门课让学生为在真实实验室里工作做好准备。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑瑞派」——先把人派到前面去等着；prepare 就是准备、预备。

root: 源自拉丁语 parare（使就绪、置办），加前缀 prae-（在前、事先）构成 praeparare，经分词 praeparatus 与古法语 preparer 进入英语；同族词有 preparation、preparatory，repair 亦出同一 parare。

sensesIntro.en: The core is readiness made in advance; the senses divide into general preparation, cooking, training people, and drawing up papers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是提前造出的就绪状态；义项由此分出一般准备、做饭配药、训练人员，以及起草文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of chopped vegetables on a board, the pan already hot, a hand reaching for the salt.
core.cn: 核心意象：案板上一排切好的菜，锅已烧热，手正把盐罐拉到近前。

branches.en: a bag packed the night before a journey
branches.cn: 出发前一夜就收拾好的包

branches.en: vegetables cut and waiting beside a hot pan
branches.cn: 切好放在热锅旁的蔬菜

branches.en: a student practising on a lab bench before the test
branches.cn: 考试前在实验台上练习的学生

branches.en: a report laid on the table before the meeting starts
branches.cn: 会议开始前摆在桌上的报告

branches.en: a cook reading the recipe once before starting
branches.cn: 开火前先把菜谱看一遍的厨师

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of readiness plus a prefix of time, and English added suffixes that turn it into a process, an adjective and a state.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示「使就绪」的拉丁动词加上时间前缀，英语又添上后缀，使它变成过程、形容词与状态。

latinIntro.en: Prepare goes back to Latin praeparare, from prae- and parare, to make ready; the participle praeparatus and the noun praeparatio carry the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: prepare 上溯拉丁语 praeparare，由 prae- 与 parare（使就绪）构成；分词 praeparatus 与名词 praeparatio 用的是同一词干。

definition_zh: 路；道路；途径
definition_en: a hard way for vehicles, or a route toward a goal
core_image: 雨后泥泞的乡间小路
scene: 雨后乡间的小路泥泞难走，他们放慢了车速。 After the rain the country road was muddy, so they drove slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 road 是「道路」（第 1 个义项：供车辆通行的路面）；句意：雨后乡间的小路泥泞难走，他们放慢了车速。

derivatives.zh: 路边
车行道
路障

senses.title: A way for vehicles
senses.definition: a hard surface built for cars and other vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 为汽车等车辆修建的坚硬路面
senses.example: The road is closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路因维修封闭。
senses.why: The road is the prepared line of travel.
senses.whyCN: 道路是修整好的通行线路。

senses.title: A journey
senses.definition: travel or a journey along a route
senses.definitionCN: 沿路线行进或旅行
senses.example: The band has been on the road for months.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队已经巡演了好几个月。
senses.why: Being on the road means being in motion.
senses.whyCN: on the road 意为一直在路上。

senses.title: A way to a goal
senses.definition: a course of action leading to a result
senses.definitionCN: 通向结果的行为路径
senses.example: Education is the road to a better life.
senses.exampleCN: 教育是通往更好生活的道路。
senses.why: A goal is reached by following a route.
senses.whyCN: 目标要沿着一条路线才能抵达。

intro.en: Road comes from Old English rād, a riding or journey, from ridan, to ride.
intro.cn: road 源自古英语 rād（骑行、旅程），来自 ridan（骑）。

items.en: Rād means a riding or journey.
items.cn: rād 意为骑行或旅程。

items.en: Road shifts from journey to the way itself.
items.cn: road 由旅程转指道路本身。

items.en: Turnpikes make roads common objects.
items.cn: 收费公路让道路成为常见事物。

items.en: On the road means travelling.
items.cn: on the road 意为在路上旅行。

items.en: Road maps guide both cars and plans.
items.cn: 路线图既指引车辆也指引计划。

note.en: A road is for vehicles; a street usually has buildings beside it.
note.cn: road 供车辆通行，street 通常两侧有建筑。

entries.definition: past tense of ride
entries.definitionCN: 骑（过去式）

entries.definition: the part for vehicles
entries.definitionCN: 车行道

entries.definition: the edge of a road
entries.definitionCN: 路边

entries.definition: a road in a town with buildings
entries.definitionCN: 街道

entries.definition: the way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 路线

entries.definition: a narrow way for walking
entries.definitionCN: 小径

normalIntro.en: A road began as the act of riding.
normalIntro.cn: road 最初指的是骑行的行为。

normal.en: The main road carries most traffic.
normal.cn: main road 承载大部分车流。

normal.en: Road safety saves lives.
normal.cn: road safety 能拯救生命。

normal.en: On the road means travelling.
normal.cn: on the road 意为在旅途中。

normal.en: A road map shows the way.
normal.cn: road map 显示路线。

normal.en: Cross the road at the lights.
normal.cn: cross the road 要在红绿灯处过。

abstract.en: Picture a wet lane shining after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后发亮的湿漉小路。

abstract.en: Imagine a band's van rolling from town to town.
abstract.cn: 想象乐队的车从小镇开往小镇。

abstract.en: Think of a long straight line toward a bright gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一条通向明亮大门的长直线。

examples.en: The road to the village is very narrow.
examples.cn: 通往村庄的路非常窄。

examples.en: They are on the road again this week.
examples.cn: 他们这周又上路了。

examples.en: Hard work is the road to success.
examples.cn: 努力是通往成功的道路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「road」听起来像「绕的」——弯来绕去让人走的，就是道路。

root: 古英语 rād（骑行、旅程）→ 行走的路线 → road，核心义「被踩出来、供人前往的路线」。

sensesIntro.en: A road is a way for vehicles, the state of travelling, or a route to a goal.
sensesIntro.cn: road 指车辆通行的道路、在旅途中的状态，或通往目标的途径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet lane shining after rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后发亮的小路。

branches.en: The built way for vehicles is the main sense.
branches.cn: 为车辆修建的路是主要义项。

branches.en: Being on the road is being in motion.
branches.cn: on the road 就是处于行进中。

branches.en: A plan also follows a road to its result.
branches.cn: 计划也沿着一条路抵达结果。

branches.en: The physical way and the journey share one line.
branches.cn: 实体的路与旅程共享同一条线。

branches.en: Travelling and striving both mean moving toward something.
branches.cn: 旅行与奋斗都意味着朝某处前进。

intro.en: Road comes from Old English rād, riding or journey.
intro.cn: road 源自古英语 rād（骑行、旅程）。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and shares a root with ride.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属于日耳曼语，与 ride 同源。

items.example: Road shifted to the way itself.

items.exampleCN: roadblock 由 road 与 block 组成。

items.meaning: map of roads or a plan
items.exampleCN: road map 延伸到计划含义。
